Sports.title: ‘A great feeling’: Mykhailo Mudryk seals loan move from Chelsea to Tottenham
Sports.content:
Tottenham have thrown a Premier League lifeline to the forgotten Chelsea winger, Mykhailo Mudryk, signing him on loan just before the transfer deadline and challenging him to revive his career.

Mudryk became a €100m (£89m) player when Chelsea took him from Shakhtar Donetsk in January 2023; the deal comprised an initial €70m and €30m in add-ons. Chelsea beat Arsenal to his signature at a point when the Ukrainian was among the most in-demand players in Europe.

The move to Chelsea did not work out and Mudryk hit rock bottom when he was banned for returning an adverse reading for the banned substance, meldonium, which can increase respiratory capacity and stamina. His last competitive game for Chelsea was on 28 November 2024.

Mudryk was suspended before being given a four-year ban by the Football Association. But after an appeal to the court of arbitration for sport, he was able to resolve his case with the FA at the end of July, being cleared for an immediate return to playing. He accepted breaking anti-doping rules and agreed to a suspension that was equal to the time he had already served. The FA noted that changes have been made to the World Anti-Doping Agency’s rules on meldonium and had Mudryk’s test been conducted today then “the concentration of meldonium in the sample would not have been reported” and no adverse finding would have been recorded.

Spurs have taken a punt on Mudryk on the recommendation of their manager, Roberto De Zerbi, who worked productively with the 25-year-old at Shakhtar, overseeing his breakthrough season in 2021-22. De Zerbi was in the market for a left winger to complete a new-look front line with the right-sided attacker Sávio and the central striker Omar Marmoush; both have joined from Manchester City.

Spurs failed with moves for Cody Gakpo and Iliman Ndiaye. The former was retained by Liverpool; the latter went from Everton to City. And so De Zerbi, who has started the season with Mathys Tel on the left, pivoted to Mudryk. The deal for him has a £75m purchase option.

“It’s a great feeling. I can’t wait to start training and playing for the club, and I’m so excited to be reunited with Roberto De Zerbi,” said Mudryk. “He’s my football father. I believe in him. I trust him. I know what he wants from me and with him I always feel I’m improving.”

Speaking during Spurs’s pre-season tour of Australia when Mudryk’s ban ended, De Zerbi said: “He’s my son. I’m very happy. He deserves to play. He’s a cool guy, a top player. Hopefully he can show what he suffered in the last two years in this next season.”

Spurs have not done business with Chelsea since 2009 when the goalkeeper, Carlo Cudicini, was allowed to join them from Stamford Bridge on a free transfer. Yet they added another Chelsea player on deadline day with the centre-half Tosin Adarabioyo signing for £7m.

Adarabioyo replaces Kevin Danso, who went to Sunderland on an initial season-long loan which will be followed by a mandatory £25m purchase. Spurs also moved the midfielder, Pape Sarr, to Juventus on an initial loan with a buy option. The deal is valued at €30m.

Sports.title: Sunderland pip Crystal Palace in battle of the private jets to land Malick Fofana
Sports.content:
Sunderland and Crystal Palace were involved in an extraordinary deadline-day tug of war that concluded with Malick Fofana agreeing to swap Lyon for the Stadium of Light in a club-record £31m move.

On Tuesday morning it had seemed that the 21-year-old Belgium winger was heading for Sunderland on a five-year contract, but then Pierre Sage led an attempt to hijack the deal. Palace’s manager coached Fofana at Lyon and forged a strong bond with a player he was keen to bring to Selhurst Park. After speaking to Sage on the phone, Fofana seemed to have changed his mind and decided he wanted to reunite with his old boss in south London. Sunderland, though, refused to surrender.

That meant Lyon had a bidding war on their hands and responded by agreeing improved deals with both clubs. Agents’ fees and Fofana’s personal terms were also understood to have risen accordingly. Meanwhile, two private jets, one dispatched by Sunderland and the other by Palace, sat on the tarmac at Lyon airport.

At one point Fofana was said to have been seen boarding the former aircraft before a flight to Newcastle airport but, in reality, he was headed to a private hospital in France for a medical commissioned jointly by Palace and Sunderland. With time running out, both clubs accepted this unusual arrangement was the only way a player targeted by Arsenal throughout much of the window would be heading to England.

In an attempt to remind Fofana, who scored 11 goals in 59 appearances for Lyon since arriving from Gent in 2024, why he had originally been so excited about playing for Régis Le Bris on Wearside, Kyril Louis-Dreyfus, Sunderland’s owner, flew to Lyon – presumably on a third jet – and spoke to him privately. It appears to have proved an inspired intervention as, shortly after 9pm, Fofana announced that he had made his choice and would be travelling to the Stadium of Light after all.

Although the initial fee agreed is £26m, add-ons dictate it should eventually rise to £31m. That leaves a forward capped five times by Belgium set to become Sunderland’s record signing, eclipsing the £30m paid to Strasbourg for midfielder Habib Diarra last summer. Sunderland have submitted a deal sheet and expect it to be concluded shortly.

Sports.title: West Ham fight off Wolves as Divine Mukasa double eases pressure on Nuno
Sports.content:
It was a match between two disjointed sides, two teams trying to carve out new identities following the drop into the Championship. In the end West Ham won thanks to a bit of luck, a degree of resolve and, crucially, a sharpness in front of goal that took them away from Wolves and reduced the pressure on Nuno Espírito Santo, for a few days at least.

First-half goals from Divine Mukasa and Jarrod Bowen, the latter from the penalty spot, were complemented by two more in the second; Mukasa secured his brace alongside a goal for Konstantinos Mavropanos. The defender doubled up himself too, albeit by scoring at his own end, as Wolves tried to claw their way back into contention. The visitors also added a decent goal from the midfielder Marshall Munetsi to their tally. For all their obvious technical ability, however, César Peixoto’s side lacked the hosts’ sang-froid at the crucial moments and that proved the decisive factor.

Nuno’s mantra after the match was “I think we can do better”, but he was clearly grateful for the win. “We all know that it was much needed,” he said. “Looking back even on today, we have mistakes again but we’ve been much more effective in our attacking actions.”

With West Ham’s uncertainty extending beyond the field of play, there was much interest taken from the appearance of Amanda Staveley in the stands here. The former Newcastle shareholder remains in the running to acquire a stake in West Ham and could be seen punching the air at Mukasa’s first-half banger. The Manchester City loanee was not the only new recruit to impress, with Arne Engels excellent alongside him in midfield.

What gave off the vibes of being an uninspiring opening half ended up being blessed by three goals. West Ham were on the back foot for much of the opening half-hour but established a two-goal lead by the 40th minute after a short spell of improved play. The opening goal was a memorable one, hit by Mukasa from 25 yards and cannoning into the net off the underside of the bar. It was a memorable way for the teenager to open his account, and it came after a piece of smart attacking play that got Kyle Walker-Peters behind Wolves’ defensive line. Seven minutes later, Bowen converted a penalty after swift feet from Joel Piroe confused André into an untimely tackle.

View image in fullscreen Jarrod Bowen doubles West Ham’s lead from the penalty spot. Photograph: Saud Ahmed/PPAUK/Shutterstock

Before Nuno could get his troops into the dressing room and preach the importance of a clean sheet, Wolves hit back. With West Ham’s defence pushing up, a fortunate deflection off the previously bewildered André opened up the opportunity for Munetsi to run into space, check inside Mavropanos and finish coolly inside Mads Hermansen’s left-hand post.

With nascent enthusiasm tempered by the late concession, the atmosphere among the home support quietened as the second half began, perhaps in anticipation of further trials for West Ham. Instead they extended their lead in short order and it was Mukasa who struck again. This was a lovely move, starting with a cute through ball from Bowen that Pablo dummied to take four Wolves players out of the equation. Receiving on the edge of the box, Mukasa stood up Toti Gomes, shifted to his left and hit a shot that deflected off the Wolves skipper and beyond the despairing José Sá.

“I’m delighted by the way he played,” Nuno said of Mukasa. “All the young lads, not just those who joined this summer, have brought us energy and talent. There’s a lot of things to improve but I’m delighted to have him.”

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Wolves responded to the third goal by grabbing hold of possession once more, but the sprightly Fer López spurned two chances. Up the other end, however, and an Engels corner was deep and dangerous and, after Mavropanos saw a towering header crash off the bar, the Greek defender smashed the rebound home on the volley. Six minutes after celebrating, Mavropanos got the final touch to a cross from Jackson Tchatchoua to turn the ball into his own net.

Wolves created no further chances, but could take solace from the performance of the full-back Tchatchoua, who looked impactful at both ends, while Mateus Mané was dominant on the left. “We created a lot of chances to score, they scored more goals,” said Peixoto. “West Ham took their chances and that’s the difference.”

Sports.title: Aston Villa sign Mbaye and Harwood-Bellis as Newcastle get Fernandez-Pardo
Sports.content:
Aston Villa completed the signings of Ibrahim Mbaye and Taylor Harwood-Bellis on deadline day, with Unai Emery confident the club’s radical summer overhaul has left Villa in position to replicate their recent success. Villa, who have lost both of their Premier League games this campaign, have qualified for the Champions League in two of the past three seasons and won their first major trophy in 30 years after lifting the Europa League.



The £47m arrival of the 18-year-old winger Mbaye from Paris Saint-Germain and £25m deal for Harwood-Bellis from Southampton represented Villa’s ninth and 10th summer signings respectively. Villa had generated more than £300m from the sales of nine players, six of whom started May’s Europa League triumph in Istanbul; Morgan Rogers, Ollie Watkins, Ezri Konsa, Youri Tielemans, Lucas Digne and Emiliano Martínez all departed Villa Park in recent weeks, Rogers and Martinez joining Chelsea.

Watkins’s £50m exit to the Saudi Pro League club Al-Hilal, after rejecting Villa’s offer of a new contract, led to Villa signing Nicolas Jackson for an initial £47.5m that could rise to a club-record £65m. Earlier in the window, Villa signed Johan Manzambi for a club-record £52m from Freiburg but the Switzerland midfielder is yet to make his debut as he continues his recovery from a knee injury he sustained at the World Cup.



After Monday’s 1-0 home defeat by Arsenal, Emery struck an upbeat tone. “We are happy how we are closing the transfer window,” said Villa’s manager. “We are not regretting anything and the players who are joining are players that should be enough to rebuild the team with the structure we want. I think we replaced the players as we planned.”



Zion Suzuki, a £30m arrival from Parma, made his Villa debut against Arsenal and Villa’s new No 1 accepts the task of replacing Martínez is a “good challenge”. “It was my priority to play games so that is why I made the decision and I played in Belgium for one year, in Parma for two years,” said the 24-year-old, who joined Villa after a move to PSG collapsed in the final stages. “In the end I am here and playing for Villa. I just wanted to come here for this club. There are so many expectations. It is not easy to play after [Martínez] but I want to help the team and be like him.



“It was very important to play in Serie A for two years and now I am confident. I made good steps and now I am here to play for the club. I want to enjoy this moment and help the team. I am really looking forward to [playing in] the Champions League but before that, I want a first Premier League win to get some momentum.”

Newcastle, meanwhile, concluded a “transformational” transfer window by securing the target that topped their shopping list in May with only hours of the transfer window remaining.

The £51m signing of the Belgium forward Matias Fernandez-Pardo from Lille on deadline day is regarded as a considerable coup and prompted boardroom celebration at the end of a turbulent summer. The 21-year-old is Newcastle’s eighth signing of a transfer window that has also seen Eddie Howe replaced as manager by Matthias Jaissle and three of the team’s biggest names – Anthony Gordon, Sandro Tonali and Bruno Guimarães – sold for a total approaching £250m.

Ross Wilson, Newcastle’s sporting director, kept in frequent contact with Fernandez-Pardo’s advisers. “Matias is a strong example of how a transfer window can unfold with twists and turns along the way,” said Wilson. “Back in May he was our top target and we always remained engaged with him. Now at the end of the window he becomes our eighth addition to a refreshed Newcastle United and we are excited to welcome him.”

View image in fullscreen Matias Fernandez-Pardo is seen as having the ability and verstatilty to be an ideal fit for Matthias Jaissle’s Newcastle. Photograph: Jean-François Badias/AP

Fernandez-Pardo’s elusive movement and ability to operate as a No 10, a No 9 or wide-left attacker explains why Newcastle were prepared to stay patient for his signature. “A lot of hours went into this one,” acknowledged Wilson. “But we’re clear on our identity and Matias has speed, intensity and work rate in abundance. We believe in his profile a great deal. Our fans will enjoy him and I know he will also enjoy our amazing St James’ Park atmosphere.”

Jaissle seemed equally delighted to have reinforced his frontline with a versatile attacker. “We were all delighted when we knew we could complete this deal,” said the German, who has made three key signings in the £39m Amar Dedic, the £52m Nico González and now Fernandez-Pardo since arriving on Tyneside in early August. “Matias is a highly technical player with explosiveness in his game. He can score and assist, he has courage and the ability to take players on. We’re sure our supporters will enjoy watching him play.”

“I’m really happy to be here and very proud to be at such a big club,” said the Belgian. “I spoke to the head coach and he really showed me how much he wanted me to be here. In terms of my career progression it made complete sense to come; I didn’t hesitate at all. I can’t wait to start my wonderful adventure here.”

Nick Woltemade’s failure to fit into Jaissle’s high-intensity gameplans explains why Germany forward, signed for £70m from Stuttgart last August, has joined Juventus on a year-long loan.

Elsewhere, Barcelona have confirmed that Gabriel Jesus has joined from Arsenal on a permanent basis for a fee that is thought to be €10m (£8.6m). The Brazil striker was in attendance for Barcelona’s 5-2 win over Rayo Vallecano on Monday night after a deal was struck over the weekend and he leaves north London as only the 12th player to win the Premier League title with two different clubs, having also done so with Manchester City.

Harvey Elliott has also joined Valencia on loan from Liverpool, while across Merseyside, Beto has sealed a £15.5m move from Everton to Fiorentina.

Kevin Danso has joined Sunderland on a year-long loan from Tottenham that should lead to a formal £25m transfer for the Austria centre-half next summer.

Fulham have completed the signing of Manuel Ángel from Real Madrid, having already signed César Palacios and Gonzalo García from the Spanish giants.

Sports.title: Football Daily | Tottenham and the rapid disappearance of their club hype man
Sports.content:
LIVE ON BIG WEBSITE

Before we get going, a reminder to join our team of writers for all the latest transfer deadline day updates before the window slams shut (in most major leagues) at 11pm BST. Get on it.

NOT SO HOT(SPURS)

While Football Daily isn’t going to claim to have looked too hard, the earliest mention we could find of Tottenham Hotspur being “in very real danger” of having to play Lincoln City home and away this season dates back to early March. Thomas Frank had been sacked a couple of weeks previously and fabled firefighter Igor Tudor had arrived in north London, only to lose his first two matches. While the weird but mercifully brief fever dream prompted a deluge of further hand-wringing, Spurs eventually avoided the drop thanks to replacing the Croat with Roberto De Zerbi. A more passable version of Red Adair, the Italian masterminded heroic wins over already-relegated Wolves, a Villa side focused entirely on Bigger Vase and an Everton team who had last done anything of interest 31 years previously. Not so much a miraculous escape, as a quite fortunate one aided by the benevolence of the fixture generator, it prompted the club hierarchy to hose cash in all directions, all the better to ensure Spurs never find themselves circling the drain again.

So how’s that going, eh? Just two top-flight games into the new campaign and De Zerbi’s much-bolstered squad is already rock bottom of the table and six points off the early pace set by their relegation rivals Hull City. And having completely embarrassed themselves at Brentford on the opening weekend of the season, you could have been forgiven for presuming their first home game of the campaign might have been prefaced by a modicum of humility. Eh? Eh? Oh. “We’ve spent and we’ve spent and we’ve spent!” whooped the designated club hype man in his pre-match address from the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium sward, a field of nightmares upon which Beyoncé has played twice as many gigs as the three league wins Spurs managed last season. “We’re back! We’re going places! We’re huge!”

Approximately 90 minutes and a third consecutive home defeat at the hands of Newcastle later, there was scarcely a peep from said hype bro, so loud was the jeering of Geordies revelling in the obvious discomfort of their former midfielder Sandro Tonali, who could scarcely have done less to justify his £100m summer fee before being hooked in raucous ignominy. “Forget the result,” cooed De Zerbi, after witnessing his side go down to goals from Anthony Elanga and Yoane Wissa. “I am not angry, we are working well and were unlucky today with the result. There is no panic. I know where we are going and what the plan is.” Of course everyone has a plan until they get the kind of smacks in the face dished out by Brentford and Newcastle but De Zerbi can at least take heart from the fact that on Saturday, Tottenham looked pretty impressive until they didn’t. It’s a minor victory that will have to do until obliging Everton come to town in two games’ time.

RECOMMENDED FOLLOWING

Now on BlueSpace, TikBook, Instachat, all the lesser disgraces.

QUOTE OF THE DAY

“It is a decision that hurts my soul but I know it is time. I love, have loved and I will always love being part of the national team. I have emptied myself: now I have nothing more to give and, besides, there are great young players coming through who deserve to be [selected]. I love you! I thank God for making me Argentinian” – Lionel Messi, with the heaviest of hearts, bids farewell to international duty.

View image in fullscreen An artist draws a painting of Lionel Messi, in Mumbai. We can’t draw for toffee so we’re in no position to criticise the likeness. Photograph: Divyakant Solanki/EPA

double quotation mark As probably the greatest player in history has announced his retirement from international football, I’d like to do likewise. Sure, the ingrates never picked me, overlooking my abilities through several World Cups and Euros, but I feel that, like Messi, the time has come to finally hang up my … ah, hopes of a call-up. But never say never, eh? Look all that happened when the little maestro changed his mind last time around! So, yes, I could still be talked out of this decision, should my country decide they need me. Thank you and …goodbye. For now, at least” – Justin Kavanagh.

double quotation mark Early days but Emi Martínez’s transfer for £7.5m seems like the bargain of the season. OK, he let in three against Brighton but saved many more and transformed Chelsea’s defence. I wonder how much they could sell Robert Sánchez on for? I predict, probably much more than £7.5m” – Nigel Sanders.

double quotation mark So August has just ended and my household is already in a contest to see ‘who can have the most miserable season’, which should cheer up anyone whose pre-season optimism has had an early blow. Me: Luton – one win from three in League One with 10 goals conceded. My wife and son: Spurs – say no more. My other son: West Ham – one win from three in the Championship. It’s going to be a long nine months” – Kevin Goddard.

If you have any, please send letters to the.boss@theguardian.com. Today’s prizeless letter o’ the day goes to … Justin Kavanagh. Terms and conditions for our competitions, when we run them, are here.

Sports.title: ‘In my heart until I die’: Argentina says a tearful thank you to Lionel Messi
Sports.content:
Anyone who was present at Lionel Scaloni’s press conference immediately after the World Cup final between Spain and Argentina in New Jersey on 19 July and saw his tears, the sobs which prevented him from speaking while he got up and walked out, could tell this was a man weeping not because of defeat in a single match but because he was fully aware that what that particular group of men had been through for the past eight years had come to an end.

Messi’s announcement that he is retiring from international football, posted on Instagram on Monday complete with photos of three handwritten sheets of some anonymous yet corporate-looking headed paper and a Harry Potter Time Turner pen, to the soundtrack of Brindis sung by Soledad Pastorutti, instantly dominated the news and unleashed a barrage of homages, gratitude and joy from all corners. But it’s not exactly a surprise.

“How crazy that the day has come, dear Leo,” Cristian Romero posted, making it clear that this was expected in spite of the unexpectedness. “The day no one wanted to arrive has arrived,” echoed Giovani Lo Celso, who said he had “nine years listening to you, admiring you and learning by your side”. His international teammates highlight how in their childhood they dreamed of meeting him one day, let alone actually playing with him. Nico Paz says since he was four years old he “used to watch you play with my dad and we would calculate together whether I would be in time to play with you”.

It’s not just his teammates who are expressing gratitude and nostalgia. On a Buenos Aires street corner someone put a red telephone on a table with a sign saying: “What would you say to Messi?” Passersby picked up the receiver and talked into it: “I’m 86 years old and you have given me the greatest joys in my life. You will be in my heart until the day I die,” one gentleman said. A young boy saw the news and “burst into tears even though I was at school”. A well-spoken woman said “we will miss you because you are an extraordinary being”, a little girl added “you’re the best and the greatest”. An old man signed off “bye, son”.

Influencers, journalists, artists, cultural commentators and psychologists all expressed their gratefulness for Messi being a great human being. “Messi led by example,” the veteran sportswriter Matías Martin wrote, while the coach and motivational speaker Matias “Coco” Gallo Bevegni posted that the World Cup winner “taught me more in defeat than in victory”.

View image in fullscreen A message written by Lionel Messi and posted to Instagram explaining his retirement from the Argentina team. Photograph: Lionel Messi/Instagram/Reuters

The football pundit Morena Beltrán could not hold back the tears as she explained to her older colleagues that for her generation there is a sense of mourning and emptiness which can only be filled by gratitude, which maybe they have already experienced, because they have seen another God. The psychoanalyst Milagros Filgueras praised the decision to hand-write the note, saying some goodbyes need the body involved. The journalist Pablo Perantuono devoted his column to the “epistolary genre”, noting that a handwritten letter in this day and age is almost a countercultural act of originality.

The writer Andrés Burgo highlighted that in 10 of the past 12 World Cups, either Maradona or Messi played, so this truly marks the “end of an era in which grandparents, parents, sons and daughters and grandchildren enjoyed an incredible privilege during almost 45 years. The heir will arrive – we hope – but right now is a time of orphanage. And gratitude.”

View image in fullscreen Argentina fans wearing T-shirts depicting Lionel Messi and Diego Maradona. Photograph: Amanda Perobelli/Reuters

Messi revealed that this letter was actually written two days after the final, a cathartic diary-like release, but that on Monday, after “[what happened with] my dad” he was more convinced than ever. The note said: “It’s a decision that hurt and continues to hurt,” but that he understands this is the moment. The poet Valeria Correa Fiz pointed out that he originally wrote “I think”, crossed it out and replaced it with “I understand”. Messi swore he always gave his all, not only these past few years when “everything was won” (he never says “I won”; it’s always “we” or “it” was won) but he has nothing left to give. He’s emptied.

The 39-year-old, however, scored four goals for Inter Miami at the weekend and continues his career at club level, where he clearly still has much to give. He is not retiring from playing football, the thing he loves most. He is retiring from Argentina.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

View image in fullscreen Messi shows off the World Cup trophy after winning the 2022 final against France. Photograph: Tom Jenkins/The Guardian

With two international dates coming up and no rival agreed, no doubt the clarification that there will be no Messi in the squad will impact on the potential fixtures. And not unlike the time when he quit Argentina before, in 2016, the country’s football is in a bit of turmoil.

The context and climate include scandals surrounding the Argentinian Football Association, the pressure by some lobbies to privatise football clubs, which are non-profit organisations, and the international furore caused by several incidents during the World Cup which have landed Argentina with some hefty fines, sanctions and suspensions.

The heaviness of the Argentina flag which for so many years visibly weighed him down, turned idyllic when it became the cloak of victory, mattered very much to his father, Jorge. Messi said he wanted to win another World Cup for him. Perhaps his death has somehow freed him from that aspect of his Argentinianness.

View image in fullscreen Supporters in Sydney, Australia, watch Messi on giant TV screens after Spain defeated Argentina in the 2026 World Cup final. Photograph: David Gray/AFP/Getty Images

And just like last time, the spontaneous visceral response from the Argentinian people is acceptance and relish at the good times lived. That inexplicable sense of pride that comes from being from the same soil as someone who is very good at something and whose magic is still untarnished by the sordid final match against Spain, or any of the criticisms directed at the squad and fans throughout the tournament. If anything, his final tears in front of the stands, like Scaloni’s tears at the press conference, are mirrored in a nation moved profoundly by the generations we have just lived through, perhaps not realising we were living through them.

The huge volume of emotive, sentimental outpouring is rather lovely, and amid it all an enduring image of three little boys walking down a Buenos Aires street with No 10 Messi shirts on their backs signals the way forward, towards a future unknown.

Sports.title: ‘I was scared to tell my old teammates’: Victoria Pelova on making leap from Arsenal to Spurs
Sports.content:
There is not the same intensity to club rivalries between women’s teams as there is between their men’s counterparts, but as the game grows that is changing. Increasingly, there is animosity from fans if a player leaves for a rival side.

Victoria Pelova’s move from Arsenal to Tottenham firmly bucks the trend, though. Despite arguably having her best years ahead of her, the 27-year-old departed with a lot of well wishes and love.

“I was really scared to tell my old teammates that I was going here,” Pelova says. “My close friends knew about it, obviously, but everyone responded so well. Everyone tells me that it reflects on the person I am. So, I’m actually really glad about that.”

Pelova has been an Arsenal fan favourite despite limited minutes in her three years at the club, during which she was hampered by an anterior cruciate ligament injury sustained on international duty in June 2024. Why is she so liked? She comes across as fun and is loved by her teammates, with a wicked and dry sense of humour.

Pelova was not worried what people would make of her move to Spurs, but the Netherlands midfielder did think about it. Ultimately, it was “an easy decision” to join Martin Ho’s squad.

“The way Martin approached me, what he said about how he sees me as a player, the videos he showed me and how he wants me to be, I’ve actually never had a coach talking like that about me. So, for me, it was a good decision. I talked a lot with my mum about it and she immediately said yes. That was actually the most important thing for me, what my mum thought.”

At the start of June, Pelova shared online that her mum had died. A carousel of moving photos of the pair through the years was captioned: “Your biggest fear was leaving me behind. My biggest fear was losing you. Rest now, Mum.”

Pelova is not ready to talk about the loss, but it sits in the background of the interview. Not having to move home as a result of her leaving Arsenal was important. “It does really help me that I have friends and family around me that take care of me,” she says.

View image in fullscreen Pelova slides in on Chelsea’s Alyssa Thompson during Arsenal’s 2-0 win at Stamford Bridge in January. Photograph: Alex Broadway/WSL Football/Getty Images

Reflecting on her spell at Arsenal, with her ACL injury coming at a time when it was believed she would start to get more playing time, she says: “There was a private situation going on, my mum was ill, and I didn’t get minutes. So, it was a really tough time and people didn’t know what I was going through.”

The goal now? “To be happy again, in football and outside football, and just day by day see how it goes.

“It sounds like I have not been happy, but I have been happy in the last year and in being with my friends. But when you’re not playing as regularly as you want to it’s inevitable that you’re not going to be totally happy, and when I’m the happiest person, I will be the best footballer I can be.”

The fresh start at Tottenham has been rejuvenating. “It’s nice to have no one know you. For me, that’s the way to go. I don’t know if I can explain it, but I feel like when everyone knows you, they focus on the things they know.”

Ho made an instant impression on Pelova. “All the coaches I’ve met are always like: ‘Oh, you can play there and there and there.’ Martin was like: ‘You’re this for me.’ He knew exactly where he wanted me and what he wanted from me. That, right away, set the tone for me and it was where and how I see myself as well. What I’ve seen so far is that he’s so detailed. He just wants to make you better. He’s very strict, but he wants to make you a better player and that’s why I’m here.”

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Weekly Sign up to Moving the Goalposts No topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Ho has “a lot” of confidence in her, and that is hugely freeing. “That’s the part I don’t have to worry about … and I can focus on other things.”

Pelova’s experience of Tottenham had been playing against them, and the more difficult that got, the more it contributed to her decision to join. “Defending was so hard,” she says of facing Spurs last season. “So, I already liked the style Martin had the team playing. I also already know Caitlin Dijkstra; I’ve known her for eight years and we lived together in Amsterdam so we know each other so well. She’s like my sister. I know Lize Kop, they’re also one of my closest friends. So, that has made the transition easy because I can always rely on them.

“I’m quite social so I’ve been trying to get to know everyone, the youngsters. It’s quite a hard job in the beginning, it’s intense, but I like it. On the pitch, you’re building relationships, pre-season is always heavy, you just need to grind, but it has been good.”

Pelova has belief in herself and her body, too. “We train really hard. That’s different to what I’m used to. So, obviously it goes up and down, but I’m confident that in a few weeks everything as a team will have progressed so much. Always with new players, it needs time. I’ve been in football a really long time so I know how it goes.”

Asked about Tottenham’s chances of disrupting things at the top, she flips the question, then says she relishes being outsiders. “You need to put us on as underdogs. The underdog position is the place to be.”

Now, Pelova is ready for the intensity of pre-season to end and for the games to begin at home against West Ham on Sunday. One, in particular, stands out, and it comes on 25 October at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium. “Please, stop pre-season,” she says with a laugh. “I just want to start. I can’t wait to play against all the teams. I can’t wait to play against Arsenal.”

Sports.title: Chelsea rage at Monaco as late move for Lamine Camara collapses at 11th hour – and Liverpool could sign him
Sports.content:
Chelsea rage at Monaco as late move for Lamine Camara collapses at 11th hour – and Liverpool could sign him

Chelsea's proposed deadline day move for Monaco midfielder Lamine Camara has fallen through.

A £47million deal had been agreed for the Senegalese midfielder to move to Stamford Bridge on a six-year contract just before the transfer window's 11pm deadline.

4 Lamine Camara's move to Chelsea has spectacularly collapsed in the dying moments of deadline day Credit: Getty

However, a late twist has now seen the Ligue 1 side pull out of the deal, with Chelsea missing out on Camara's signature, as well as a direct replacement for the departed Enzo Fernandez.

And the collapsed move appears to have come about in dramatic circumstances, with Premier League rivals Liverpool understood to have had an impact on proceedings.

According to talkSPORT's Ben Jacobs, the Reds instructed Camara to wait, suggesting a move for the 22-year-old could be forthcoming next summer.

talkSPORT understands Liverpool did not directly interfere with the negotiations between Chelsea and Monaco.

Monaco turned their back on a deal, leaving Chelsea infuriated.

A Blues source told talkSPORT: "Monaco have acted in a deeply unprofessional away."

Jacobs also revealed that Monaco are now looking for an increased £60m fee to part with Camara.

Chelsea miss out on midfield target

Chelsea had looked set to bolster their midfield with Camara's proposed arrival, as they prepared to replace Enzo Fernandez.

After months of speculation surrounding his future, the Argentina star's joint-Premier League record £125million transfer to Manchester City was confirmed minutes after the 11pm transfer deadline passed,

There had been plenty of uncertainty over Camara's Monaco departure before a fee was agreed with Chelsea, with teammate Folarin Balogun's proposed move to Everton having a major impact.

4 Camara had been lined up as a replacement for Fernandez, who has joined Man City Credit: Getty

4 Camara will be going nowhere for the time being Credit: AFP

Needing to sell players to balance the books, complications over Balogun's departure left the Ligue 1 side sweating over a much-needed sale, only for another dramatic late U-turn.

Now, with Camara set to remain in French football, this has paved the way for Everton to complete the deadline day signing of the USA international.

As for Chelsea, the late turnaround sees them end the transfer window without securing the signing of an extra midfielder.

Roma's Manu Kone had also emerged as a potential option, but talkSPORT revealed that the Serie A side's manager Gian Piero Gasperini was blocking a departure for the Frenchman.

It marked an eventful transfer deadline day for Chelsea, which began with goalkeeper Robert Sanchez joining Como on loan.

The goalkeeper had been bumped down to Stamford Bridge following the arrival of Emi Martinez from Aston Villa.

4 Lamine Camara will be going nowhere for the time being

Elsewhere, midfielder Dario Essugo completed a season-long loan move to sister club Strasbourg, after a move to Hull fell through.

But after the biggest business saw Fernandez finally join Man City, Chelsea are left seething after failing to land their ideal replacement in Camara at the 11th hour.

Sports.title: Wrexham terminate triple promotion hero’s contract before transfer deadline
Sports.content:
Wrexham have mutually terminated the contract of midfielder Elliot Lee.

The 31-year-old arrived at the Welsh club from Luton Town in 2022 and quickly became a fan favourite.



3 Elliot Lee leaves Wrexham after a fairytale four-year spell at the Racecourse Ground Credit: Getty

He played a key role in the Red Dragons’ meteoric rise from the wilderness to their current standing as an established Championship club.

Lee, who was into the final year of his deal, clocked up an impressive 152 appearances for the club but found minutes hard to come by last season.

He leaves Wrexham as a free agent having netted 41 times for the club across all competitions.



Boss Phil Parkinson paid an emotional tribute to the outgoing star and even found time to pitch him to possible suitors.

Parkinson's well wishes

"I'd like to thank Elliot for what he has done for this football club.,” Parkinson said.



"He has been a great player for us here at Wrexham and has made a significant contribution to the club's rise through the divisions.

"He is at the stage now where he is eager to go and play and get some minutes, and whoever gets him will get a player who still has a lot to offer."



League One club Sheffield Wednesday are understood to be interested in bringing Lee to Hillsborough as they plot an immediate return to the Championship.

The midfielder featured heavily during Wrexham's unprecedented three-consecutive promotions between the National League and the Championship.

His performances saw him pick up a number of individual accolades along the way.

3 Wrexham boss Phil Parkinson heaped huge praise on Lee's impact at the club Credit: Getty



Lee, son of former Premier League midfielder Rob Lee, was selected in the 2022/23 National League Team of the Year.

He repeated the feat 12 months later when he was named in the League Two Team of the Season and the Professional Footballers' Association Team of the Year.

But as Wrexham moved further up the football pyramid, Lee’s game time was significantly reduced.

He made just three appearances last season, all coming in the EFL Cup.



It led to him joining Doncaster Rovers on loan where he went on to play 18 times.

Lee began his career at West Ham where he was loaned out on five separte ocassions.

3 Lee was instrumental in the club's rise from non-league to the second tier of English football Credit: Getty

After failing to make a breakthrough at the London Stadium, he was sold to Barnsley before securing a move to Luton 12 month later.

Sports.title: Enzo Fernandez gives emotional goodbye to Chelsea fans as he completes record Man City move
Sports.content:
Enzo Fernandez gives emotional goodbye to Chelsea fans as he completes record Man City move

Enzo Fernandez has issued a heartfelt statement to Chelsea fans as he completes his record-equalling move to Manchester City.

City will pay the Blues £125million for Fernandez's services, which equals a record Premier League transfer.

4 Fernandez had his heart set on a move to Real Madrid but will join City Credit: Getty

Earlier in the day a £120m deal was rejected but the two clubs are settled on £125m, which equals the Premier League record fee Liverpool spent to sign Alexander Isak last summer.

New City boss Maresca has been the driving force behind City's interest in Fernandez.

Chelsea previously set a deadline of 5pm on Friday, August 14 for interested clubs to meet their £120million asking price. However, the cut-off point passed without City making an offer.

Despite Chelsea's stance, the deal accelerated during the final hours of the transfer window and was announced shortly after the 11pm deadline.

Fernandez Chelsea departure statement

While the move is yet to be announced by either club, Fernandez posted his goodbye to Chelsea fans in an emotional statement.

Fernandez posted on Instagram: "I want you to know that these have not been easy days for me. Writing this is not easy either. The truth is, I haven’t been in a good place.

"Three years ago, Cobham and Stamford Bridge became home for me and my family. I grew attached to the people, to the shirt, and to the badge of this incredible club.

"Believe me when I say that, from the moment I arrived, I became obsessed with winning and with bringing this club every trophy that its history deserves.

"We suffered, we cried, I got angry many times, but we also celebrated titles and unforgettable victories. Together, through the good times and the difficult ones.

"I live football the same way I live my life: with passion and with all my heart. That is why I want you to know that I understand you. I truly understand you, from the bottom of my heart.

4 Fernandez reunites with his former boss at Chelsea, Maresca Credit: Getty

"But life is about making decisions, and right now I find myself having to make one of those difficult decisions. I’ve said it before, but I want to say it again: I have grown incredibly fond of this club.

"Chelsea will always have a place in my thoughts and, above all, in my heart.

"But I also understand how football works. I know how passionate you are, because I am the same. And if I were in your position, I would probably be thinking the same way.

"I want to thank every single one of you: the staff, the coaching team, the medical team, the physios, and everyone who works at Cobham and throughout this great institution.

"To all my teammates over these years, thank you from the bottom of my heart for sharing so many moments with me. I was truly happy here, and I wish you nothing but the very best for the future.

"Thank you for all the love and support you have given me and my family throughout these years. I will never forget it.

4

"This group will give you many more reasons to be happy, and I will be happy for you too. Never doubt that.

"You will always be in my heart, Blues. I will always wish you, always, nothing but the very best.

"Always Blue. Thank you, Chelsea."

Deadline day frustration

Chelsea believed they had found a replacement for Fernandez but were left stunned in the dying moments of deadline day when a move for Lamine Camara fell through.

The Blues appeared set to tie up a £47m deal for the Monaco midfielder after the Ligue 1 club had earlier seen Folarin Balogun's move to Everton fall through.

But in a crazy turn of events, Everton revived their interest in the USA striker only to see the Principality club seemingly pull the plug on the Camara deal.

4 Camara's move to Chelsea has spectacularly collapsed in the dying moments of deadline day Credit: Getty

The Senegal international had agreed a six-year deal at Stamford Bridge with the option of a further 12 months.

He was due to fly to London for his medical on Wednesday.

Monaco's stance in pulling out of the deal has left Chelsea chiefs furious.

The club view the situation as 'deeply unprofessional' and 'not the way to conduct business'.

Camara's failure to join Chelsea opens up potential for Liverpool to sign him next summer with the Reds understood to have contacted the player's camp.

To add insult to injury, talkSPORT has learnt that Chelsea had the chance to block Fernandez's move to City but opted to stick to their word, unlike Monaco.

Sports.title: Jack Grealish seals return to former club as late deal with Man City struck
Sports.content:
Jack Grealish seals return to former club as late deal with Man City struck

Jack Grealish has rejoined Everton on another season-long loan from Manchester City

The England forward is returning to Merseyside after the two clubs reached an agreement that will see the Toffees cover 90 per cent of the player's wages.

4 Grealish has been back in action for Man City early this term Credit: Getty

Having completed his medical this morning, Everton confirmed Grealish's arrival an hour before the end of the transfer window.

It brings an end to a summer of speculation over the 30-year-old's future, who also had the option of making a return to boyhood club Aston Villa.

While the transfer is a loan, it effectively spells the end of Grealish’s City career as he’s in the final year of his Etihad Stadium contract.

After his loan move was confirmed, Grealish. shared his delight at returning to Everton.

He told the club's official website: "It feels so good. I'm so happy.

"I think I'm at my best at everything in life, not just football, when I feel loved. That's what the manager has given me, what my teammates have given me and especially what the fans have given me.

"Every time I see an Everton fan, it's just pure love and the way they've welcomed me since that first game against Leeds, I'll never forget that. It means a lot to me and hopefully I've made a few Everton fans happy.

"I had a perfect time here for the first six months, then I stayed around after I got injured. I’ve been watching all the Everton games in pre-season and since the season started.

"Now I feel ready to go. I'm ready to start training tomorrow and prepare for the games."

The race for Grealish

talkSPORT reported last week that both Everton and Aston Villa – Grealish's boyhood club where he broke through and ultimately caught the attention of Man City – were interested in a loan deal.

4 Grealish enjoyed a new lease of life during his loan spell with Everton Credit: Getty

City sources denied an official approach from Sunderland amid reports of an enquiry.

With Grealish out of contract at the end of the season, City would have preferred to sell him in order to avoid losing him on a free transfer next summer.

City boss Enzo Maresca previously suggested there could be a role for Grealish at the club, but he also didn't rule out a departure for the 39-cap England international.

"He is here and it is my duty to coach Jack and to try to get the best," he said after City's win over Bournemouth in the opening weekend of the Premier League season.

"Then it is one more week to go [until the end of the transfer window] and we will see what happens. Not only with Jack but also other players."

Everton move helped Grealish bounce back

Grealish left on loan for Everton last August in search of more playing time, having been left out of Pep Guardiola's City's squad for the Club World Cup.

4 Grealish sparked hope of a Man City revival after featuring for them at the start of the new season Credit: Getty

And he looked to be getting back towards his best for David Moyes' side, setting up two goals on his first start.

In September, he won the league's Player of the Month award for the first time in his career.

However, a foot injury he picked up against Villa in January ended his campaign prematurely.

Grealish said he was 'gutted' to be ruled out for the remainder of the season amid form that, had it continued, might have seen him make England's World Cup squad.

Nonetheless, he finished with six Premier League assists and two goals to his name in 2025/26, a strong return all things considered.

Grealish's City struggles

Grealish joined City from Villa for £100m in the summer of 2021, making him the most expensive British player ever at the time.

4 Grealish is looking to continue the resurgent form he discovered with Everton last season Credit: Getty

He went on to make the best part of 100 appearances in all competitions across his first two seasons with Guardiola's men, winning back-to-back Premier League titles and helping City to the treble in 2022/23 – before another Premier League crown followed in 2023/24.

But he generally hasn't hit the same heights for City as he did during his breakout years at Villa, and a move away could well be necessary to kickstart his career – as his time at Everton showed.

Sports.title: EFL player has contract ripped up hours before match on his birthday
Sports.content:
EFL player has contract ripped up hours before match on his birthday

Birmingham City have terminated Jack Robinson’s contract by mutual consent on what is his 33rd birthday.

The defender leaves the Blues just 12 months into a two-year deal.

3 Jack Robinson has had an eventful birthday for the second successive year Credit: Getty

Bizarrely, Robinson secured a move to St Andrews on the exact same day last year meaning he was signed and released on consecutive birthdays.

Robinson's nightmare Birmingham spell

Robinson, who signed from Sheffield United a year ago, has struggled to find his best form since arriving at the Midlands club.

He was dismissed in just his second game for the club against local rivals Coventry City.

And it got worse for the centre-back when he received another red card two games later in a league fixture against Hull City.

Things went from bad to worse for Robinson when he scored an own goal and conceded a penalty against former club Sheffield United.

Robinson represented Birmingham just 16 times in what was a lively stint at the club.

Birmingham announced his departure on X writing: “The club can confirm that Jack Robinson has left the Club following the mutual termination of his contract.

“Everyone at Blues would like to thank Jack for his efforts while at the Club and wish him well for the future.”

The decision to part ways came just hours before Birmingham Championship clash at home to Southampton, with the match finishing 1-1.

The Blues went into the match buoyed by Friday’s 2-1 win at Wrexham – their first win of the season.

3 Robinson was sent off twice within his first four games for the club Credit: Getty

3 The Blues have secured a season-long loan for Hull's Liam Millar Credit: Getty

Birmingham boss Chris Davies received some positive news during his side's clash against the Saints with the news that Liam Millar had joined the club on a season-long loan deal.

The Hull City star, who featured for Canada at this summer’s World Cup, played a key role in the Tigers’ Championship play-off triumph last season.

He made 38 appearances for Hull last season, scoring three goals and registering five assists.

The 26-year-old played in Hull’s Premier League opening weekend victory over Manchester United.

He then scored the winner in Saturday’s 1-0 win at Coventry to hand Hull maximum points from their opening two fixtures.

The Canadian has clocked up 44 caps for his country and featured in three of their five World Cup matches.

Sports.title: Man United make bonkers deadline day enquiry for Man City player
Sports.content:
Manchester United made an audacious deadline day enquiry for Manchester City left-back Rayan Ait-Nouri, talkSPORT understands.

The Red Devils have been looking to strengthen at left-back all summer but to no avail, and they approached one of their biggest rivals in the closing stages of the transfer window.



4 Ait-Nouri has been the subject of a shock approach from Man United Credit: Getty

It is understood that talks for Ait-Nouri to move across Manchester only progressed as far as an enquiry.

Man City sources never believed that there would be any progress on a potential deal.

Ait-Nouri has struggled for minutes since completing a £32million move to the Etihad Stadium last summer.



The Algerian made just 17 Premier League appearances for the Citizens last term following his arrival from Wolves.

He is yet to feature at all for City this season, having been on the bench for all four of their opening games, with Josko Gvardiol, Nico O’Reilly and Rico Lewis all capable of playing in the left-back role.



Man United's search for a left-back

With a shock switch to Old Trafford ruled out for Ait-Nouri, Man United will likely have to look elsewhere in future windows.

Luke Shaw is currently their only specialist in the position, and Michael Carrick's side have been unsuccessful in their attempts to land no.1 target in Newcastle's Lewis Hall.



talkSPORT recently reported that United were interested in signing Barcelona full-back Alejandro Balde as an alternative.

However, the two clubs have struggled to agree on a deal, with Barca slapping a €45million (£38.5m) asking price on the Spaniard, while the Red Devils would have preferred a loan move.

As well as Balde, United have also been credited with an interest in Fulham's Antonee Robinson and RB Leipzig defender David Raum.

4 Michael Carrick is yet to sign a left-back in his first transfer window as Man United boss Credit: Getty



4 Shaw has shouldered the bulk of United's playing demands at left-back for the past year Credit: Getty

Left-back became a priority position for Man United this summer, with Shaw shouldering the responsibility in the role in the 2025/26 campaign.

But with Champions League football returning to Old Trafford this season, Michael Carrick may have too thin a squad.

The need to strengthen in this area was plain to see last Sunday, as Shaw struggled in United's 5-2 win over Ipswich.



Although the Red Devils won comfortably in the end, they had a scare when Leif Davis put the Tractor Boys ahead after Abdul Fatawu picked up the ball on the right and drove past Shaw to tee up the opener.

The England defender's fault in the goal drew criticism from talkSPORT's Alex Crook, who labelled him 'part of the problem' in United's back line.

Rayan Ait-Nouri's career

Ait-Nouri would certainly have offered plenty of Premier League experience at Old Trafford.

4 Ait-Nouri built a strong reputation for himself whilst at Wolves Credit: Getty



The 25-year-old broke into senior football with Angers in France, before signing with Wolves on an initial loan deal in 2020, before making the move permanent a year later.

He made 135 league appearances at Molineux before making the switch to the Etihad.

While he struggled for minutes at club level last season, he impressed at the World Cup, where he featured for Algeria as they reached the Round of 32 before being knocked out by Switzerland.

Despite being born in France, he has been capped 34 times by the North African nation.

Sports.title: Ben Chilwell makes shock Premier League return in deadline day move out of nowhere
Sports.content:
Ben Chilwell makes shock Premier League return in deadline day move out of nowhere

Crystal Palace have completed the signing of former Chelsea defender Ben Chilwell on a free transfer.

The England left-back joined BlueCo-owned Strasbourg on Transfer Deadline Day last year, having fallen out of favour at Stamford Bridge.

4 Chilwell provided two assists in 20 Ligue 1 appearances for Strasbourg last term Credit: Getty

Chilwell penned a two-year deal with the Ligue 1 side last year, almost a year on from his last appearance for Chelsea.

The defender was frozen out by former Blues boss Enzo Maresca, and spent the second half of the 2024/25 season on loan at Crystal Palace.

Familiar face

Palace have now brought Chilwell back to Selhurst Park for the 29-year-old, signing him on a permanent deal on deadline day.

Palace's interest in the defender comes as they continue to assess their options ahead of the end of the transfer window.

They hope to wrap up deals for Chilean winger Dario Osorio as well as the twin brother of Arsenal defender Jurrien Timber, Quentin.

The south London outfit have been in a period of transition this summer, with Pierre Sage taking over from Oliver Glasner in the dugout.

They have had to deal with major departures too, with Maxence Lacroix moved to Chelsea in a deal worth £52million, before Daniel Munoz left to join Glasner at Nottingham Forest.

Palace have strengthened their back line by bringing in proven Premier League experience in Takehiro Tomiyasu and Axel Disasi.

But after losing their opening two league games under Sage, they have bolstered their ranks further by making a late play for Chilwell.

During his loan spell at the club in 2025, he made 11 appearances and completed a Premier League game just once.

4 Chilwell scored once in his 2025 loan spell at Crystal Palace

4 Sage has had a tough start to life in English football Credit: Getty

Ben Chilwell's career

Chilwell comes back to English football after just a year at Strasbourg.

The Leicester academy graduate was one of six players to depart Chelsea to join their Ligue 1 sister club last summer, as he was convinced to join the club by then manager Liam Rosenior.

He enjoyed a resurgence campaign at Strasbourg, making 34 appearances in all competitions - his most since the 2020/21 season.

Chilwell also played a significant role in Strasbourg's historic Conference League run, featuring nine times as they reached their first ever European semi-final before being beaten by Rayo Vallecano in the last four.

The defender first made a name for himself at Leicester, as he graduated from the club's youth ranks to become a highly-rated left-back in the Premier League.

He made 123 appearances for the Foxes, scoring four goals, and made his senior England debut in 2018 whilst at the club.

4 Chilwell finally departed Chelsea last year, having been deemed as surplus to requirements at Stamford Bridge Credit: PA

In 2020, Chilwell joined Chelsea in a deal worth up to £50million, penning a five year deal.

His first season at Stamford Bridge was his most successful, as he featured 43 times in all competitions - including playing ten games in the Blues' victorious Champions League campaign.

However, Chilwell's time in west London was hampered by injuries, which caused him to miss 110 games in his five years at the club.

The arrival of Enzo Maresca as head coach in the summer of 2024 all but spelled the end of his Chelsea career, as he played just once under the Italian in the Carabao Cup before leaving to join Palace on loan, with his permanent exit following last summer.

Sports.title: Man City complete Enzo Fernandez deal: Chelsea star FINALLY gets his move for joint-record British transfer fee of £125m as Blues cave in to rivals despite signing no replacement
Sports.content:
Man City complete Enzo Fernandez deal: Chelsea star FINALLY gets his move for joint-record British transfer fee of £125m as Blues cave in to rivals despite signing no replacement

Follow all the latest deadline day news and deals with Daily Mail Sport's live blog HERE

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Manchester City struck a £125million deadline-day deal to secure Enzo Fernandez from Chelsea – but Xabi Alonso's side were left seething after Monaco pulled the plug on their own agreement for his replacement Lamine Camara.

The Fernandez sale equals the British transfer record which was paid to Newcastle by Liverpool for Alexander Isak last summer, and is a fixed fee for the 25-year-old Argentinian with no add-ons involved. He was Enzo Maresca's top target in this window.

While Chelsea reached an agreement which took their incomings towards the £500m mark for the summer – with club sources pointing out that is also a British record – they did so without having their own replacement at the ready.

Chelsea thought they had secured Camara from Monaco with less than two hours of deadline day remaining, having agreed a £47m deal. However, in a dramatic twist, the Blues were left stunned and furious when Monaco then went back on their word as the 11pm deadline approached.

Chelsea sources say the two clubs had reached a full, written, club-to-club agreement for Camara to join. Yet when Monaco renegotiated their transfer of Folarin Balogun to Everton, Chelsea were told that the deal for Camara was being withdrawn.

Insiders at Stamford Bridge described it as a deeply unprofessional way for another club to conduct business.

That meant Chelsea were left without cover for Fernandez. Blues sources added they had the opportunity to stop Fernandez from joining City after they learned of the U-turn on Camara – but they had given their word to their Premier League counterparts and, unlike Monaco, they honoured it.

Chelsea had spent their deadline day chasing Camara, seeing two bids worth £38.5m and £42.9m turned down earlier in the day before having a third accepted.

Manchester City have reached an agreement with Chelsea for the signing of Enzo Fernandez

In a statement released around the same as this bombshell news broke, Fernandez said to his former fans: ‘Chelsea will always have a place in my thoughts and, above all, in my heart. But I also understand how football works. I know how passionate you are, because I am the same. And if I were in your position, I would probably be thinking the same way.’

City leaving their club-to-club negotiations until the final two days of the window had left Chelsea with limited time to secure their own signing.

Central to Chelsea agreeing to a deal with City was Fernandez’s relationship with Maresca with the two wanting to work together again. Fernandez was known to have been keen to leave, having flirted with that idea before the last season had even finished.

With no Fernandez or Camara – and with Dario Essugo joining Strasbourg on loan – Chelsea’s senior midfield options are Moises Caicedo, Reece James, Romeo Lavia, Valentin Barco and Jordan Henderson. Malo Gusto can also be used centrally if required. While Fernandez developed a helpful habit of scoring important goals, Xabi Alonso has an impressive attack, having signed Morgan Rogers for £117m this summer to form a front three with Cole Palmer and Joao Pedro.

Chelsea fans may be glad that what turned into an exhausting saga is coming to an end at least.

Chelsea initially attempted to accelerate a conclusion by creating their own deadline for bids by Friday August 14 at 5pm. That was for a £120m transfer and the terms were communicated to their Premier League counterparts via Fernandez’s camp, led by Javier Pastore. Chelsea’s hope was that it would give them ample time to replace their 2022 World Cup-winning midfielder.

However, City did not play along with Chelsea’s deadline. No offer was submitted, and Blues insiders claimed they ‘expected’ Fernandez to stay with them for the entirety of 2026-27.

He was even handed the captain’s armband when he appeared as a substitute in their final friendly at home to Real Sociedad, receiving a mixed reception inside Stamford Bridge.

Fernandez appeared in their Premier League opener at Fulham as a substitute. While the home fans inside Craven Cottage booed him after Argentina’s behaviour at the World Cup, the away end welcomed him warmly, with those Chelsea supporters even chanting his name.

Fernandez continued to train with his team-mates and in Alonso’s main squad rather than the second group including Liam Delap and Nicolas Jackson, but then disappeared.

Following talks with Alonso, he was not involved in their Carabao Cup win over Luton, or in their Premier League victory against Brighton. Alonso insisted publicly it was his decision after speaking with the player, but did add he selected a squad that had the ‘desire to play’.

Maresca had a good relationship with Fernandez at Chelsea, where he often wore the captain’s armband in the absence of James. Maresca also handed him that armband barely a month after the Argentinian was accused of singing a racist song following his country’s 2024 Copa America triumph. That was in Chelsea’s Premier League opener at home to City.

When Maresca eventually exited Chelsea after speaking with City about succeeding Pep Guardiola, Fernandez was among those who spoke up, suggesting it ‘hurt’ the team. The Blues ended up finishing 10th in that season, leaving them with no European football under Alonso for this term.
