World.title: US dollar exchange rate stabilizes in Baghdad, rises in Erbil
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The exchange rate of the US dollar against the Iraqi dinar remained stable on Tuesday in Baghdad, the capital of Iraq, while it experienced a slight increase in Erbil, the capital of the Kurdistan region.

The US dollar exchange rate stabilized at 1,542.5 Iraqi dinars in Baghdad’s Al-Kifah and Al-Harithiya stock exchanges throughout the day.

The exchange rate in currency exchange shops in Baghdad remained stable, ranging between 1,547.5 Iraqi dinars and 1,537.5 Iraqi dinars, Shafaq News reported.

In Erbil, the US dollar exchange rate increased slightly, fluctuating between 1,542 and 1,541.5 Iraqi dinars.

The Central Bank of Iraq (CBI) said in February 2023 that it has begun using the new US dollar exchange rate of 1,300 dinars to every US dollar.

The previous official exchange rate was 1,450 dinars to one US dollar, which was being exchanged in the parallel market at a rate of 1,550 dinars.

While the official exchange rate was 1,450 dinars per dollar in January 2023, the US currency was being exchanged at 1,610 dinars during the same month in the parallel market in Iraq. This variation represented more than a 10 percent difference in exchange rates.

World.title: Iraqi PM calls for boosting oil output to 10 million bpd by 2030
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi called on Tuesday for an increase in oil output to reach 10 million barrels per day by 2030.

Al-Zaidi’s remarks took place during a meeting held to discuss the country’s strategic plan to develop and increase oil production, according to a statement released by the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO).

According to al-Zaidi, Iraq’s oil output should be proportionate to its reserves, oil production capabilities, and the growing number of the population, allowing it to satisfy its residents’ needs as well as development requirements.

The prime minister indicated that it is important to improve infrastructure and export capacity to meet the expected rise in output.

Iraq’s oil production reached approximately 4.5 million barrels per day by the end of 2025.

Al-Zaidi directed an increase in output from oil fields in the Kurdistan region of Iraq and the expansion of exploration activities to achieve the plan’s objectives and reach a production capacity of 10 million barrels per day by 2030.

The prime minister also instructed the full recovery of associated gas to fulfill domestic energy demands, prevent waste, and eventually eliminate the need for imports.

According to al-Zaidi, the Oil Ministry will invite major foreign oil firms to a conference to attract investments, expertise, and technologies.

The Iraqi Oil Ministry is anticipated to reach deals with oil corporations to conduct exploration, production, development, and export projects, therefore improving the country’s position in the global energy market and bolstering its resources and economic capacity.

World.title: China-Nepal flood toll tops 1,000 as tunnel rescue offers last hope
World.content:
Nuwakot – The death toll from devastating Himalayan glacial floods crossed the grim 1,000 mark on Tuesday, as Chinese and Nepali teams searched for survivors including dozens feared trapped in hydropower tunnels.

Nearly 4,500 people are missing after the gigantic wave of freezing water, rocks and debris triggered by a high-altitude glacial collapse roared downstream on Wednesday, wiping out entire settlements and carving a path of destruction across Nepal.

Nepali rescue teams are digging, drilling and blasting through debris in a desperate race against time to free around 100 hydropower workers believed trapped in multiple tunnels.

So far, rescuers have recovered only bodies from tunnels blocked by sludge, and hopes of finding survivors are fading.

Excavators worked into the night on Tuesday, but an army update noted that “a large amount of water started flowing” into a hole they were digging, forcing them to start a new opening.

Nepal’s Prime Minister Balendra Shah has called the catastrophe “unimaginable and heartbreaking”.

With mortuaries overflowing in Nepal, authorities have begun burying hundreds of unidentified bodies after DNA sampling.

At least 17 bodies have also been pulled from rivers downstream in India.

Police, using a drone to search for survivors, said on Tuesday that they had located 24 corpses inside a single house in Nuwakot district.

Foreign Minister Shisir Khanal said he still hoped some of the thousands missing could be alive.

“Miracles do happen,” he told AFP in an interview. “At this point, I do not want to completely give up hope.”

– ‘Find their bodies’ –

In the capital Kathmandu, crowds lined up to search for their missing relatives.

Debu Sapkota, a 58-year-old driver, posted photos of his 83-year-old mother-in-law and her granddaughter, alongside dozens of others.

Sapkota said he had little hope they survived after witnesses saw them being carried away by the torrent.

“I am here hoping to find their bodies,” he said

Some, believing they will never find their missing relatives, held symbolic funerals in accordance with Nepali Hindu customs.

“We searched everywhere, went to morgues across the country, but could not find his body,” said Jeevan Shrestha, as his 12-year-old nephew set fire to a tiny straw effigy representing his missing father.

Aid needs are enormous. Entire communities have been swept away, leaving families homeless and using makeshift shelters as heavy rain lashes down.

Roads and dozens of bridges have been smashed, and power plants destroyed.

“There are too many challenges,” said police officer E. Hawadi in badly affected Nuwakot district.

– Climate change –

AFP photographers in Nuwakot on Tuesday saw people scouring through mud for usable items and stringing up plastic sheeting for shelter in ruins.

Foreigners missing among the list include 583 in Nepal and 261 in China, coming from more than 30 nations.

They include tourists who had come for trekking in the Himalayas, as well as Hindu pilgrims seeking spiritual peace at Tibet’s sacred Mount Kailash.

Nepal’s economy is already under pressure, with limited resources to respond to a disaster of this scale.

Kathmandu has warned reconstruction costs could run into the “billions of dollars”.

There is growing anger at the scale of destruction to hit Nepal, a largely rural nation of 30 million people.

The country has contributed little to the greenhouse gas emissions driving global warming, but is among those suffering its consequences.

Khanal, the foreign minister, told AFP that the “disaster should be seen as a warning signal to the risk that climate change poses to Nepal”, adding that support should be seen “from a perspective of climate justice”.

Scientists say the Himalayas, the world’s highest mountain range, are warming rapidly as global temperatures rise, accelerating glacier melt.

Glaciers in the wider Himalayan and Hindu Kush ranges are a crucial water source for around 240 million people in the mountainous regions, as well as for another 1.65 billion people in the South Asian and Southeast Asian river valleys below.

“It impacts the entirety of the Himalayan region’s civilisation,” Khanal said.

– ‘Mourn the victims’ –

Nepal said 1,050 bodies had been recovered by Tuesday, while 3,916 people remained missing.

China’s state media reported 16 dead and 546 missing.

That takes the overall number of reported dead to 1,066 and missing to 4,462.

In China, Tibet is largely inaccessible to foreign journalists, and Chinese authorities are the only source of official information.

More than 2,000 people are aiding rescue operations, including soldiers, Xinhua added.

It said on Tuesday that teams were “working around the clock to search for survivors, repair roads, set up communication base stations and restore power lines”.

Tibetan advocacy groups in exile have questioned China’s account of the disaster, but Beijing insists that the “release of information has been open, transparent and timely”.

World.title: China’s Xi arrives in Egypt as US sanctions threat looms over Iran links
World.content:
Cairo – Chinese President Xi Jinping arrived in Egypt on Tuesday on a rare trip to the Middle East as both countries face the threat of US sanctions over financial links to Iran.

Xi and his wife were greeted on the tarmac by Egyptian President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi and the first lady, as well as a performance by an Egyptian folk dance troupe.

The two-day visit comes as both countries seek to manage the fallout of the months-long Middle East war, which began when the United States and Israel launched strikes against Iran on February 28, throwing the crucial trade region into crisis.

Washington vowed last month to destabilise Iran economically, warning of expanded sanctions against Tehran’s backers and partners that could hit Egyptian and Chinese banks, among others.

Xi’s visit “comes at a time when China’s economic interests are directly exposed to the US-Iran war”, said Gamal Salama, political science professor at Egypt’s Suez University.

China, a major buyer of Iranian oil, has presented itself as a neutral party in the Middle East conflict, repeatedly calling for a lasting ceasefire.

Egypt, a long-time recipient of US military aid, warned against regional escalation after a drone strike hit one of its ports in July.

China is “clearly seeking Egypt’s cooperation in managing and shaping regional affairs”, said Liu Jia, a research fellow at the Singapore-based Middle East Institute.

Beijing works closely with regional actors such as Egypt, which mediates between Israel and Palestinian groups, Liu added.

Both China and Egypt support an independent Palestinian state as part of a two-state solution.

“China sees Cairo as a strategic power broker,” said Salama.

Egypt’s “relations with both Washington and regional actors give Beijing both political access and diplomatic leverage across a region where China wants a much greater say,” he added.

– ‘Renewing the friendship’ –

As part of its economic pressure campaign targeting Iran, Washington last week said it would cut off the operations of Egypt’s Banque Misr in the UAE from the US financial system.

China, in response to the US measures and threats, has vowed to safeguard its interests.

Beijing has also sought to shore up ties with US-friendly regional nations ahead of a meeting between Xi and US President Donald Trump expected this month.

The Chinese and Egyptian militaries carried out joint air combat exercises in August that featured Beijing’s powerful J-16 fighter jet.

Xi’s meeting with his Egyptian counterpart Sisi, scheduled for Wednesday, follows a visit to Beijing by Jordan’s King Abdullah II, whose country has also been caught up in the US war with Iran.

Xi and Sisi are expected to discuss issues including the Gaza war, Iran, and shipping in the Red Sea and the Strait of Hormuz, according to Egyptian media.

“I look forward to renewing the friendship and working together with President Sisi to… map out a new blueprint for deepening the China-Egypt comprehensive strategic partnership,” Xi wrote in an editorial published in Egyptian media on Tuesday.

The Chinese leader’s first visit to Egypt in a decade comes as the two nations mark 70 years of diplomatic ties.

China is a major exporter to Egypt, with its trade surplus reaching $12 billion in the first seven months of 2026, according to Chinese customs data.

The leaders are expected to sign agreements on artificial intelligence, transport, energy and investment in the Suez Canal Economic Zone, Egyptian media reported.

The meeting with Xi sets Cairo up to land Chinese investments in its local AI and electronics industries, political scientist Salama said.

“What Egypt is seeking is strategic autonomy: not breaking with Washington, not aligning completely with Beijing, but creating enough room to pursue its own national interests,” he added.

World.title: IMF reaches agreement with Senegal on new $2.2 bn loan programme
World.content:
Dakar – The International Monetary Fund announced an agreement with Senegal on Tuesday for a new $2.2-billion loan programme, after a prior deal was suspended following the discovery of previously unreported debt.

The announcement comes nearly two years after Senegal’s current government, which rose to power on an opposition electoral victory, accused the former administration of ex-president Macky Sall (2012-2024) of having concealed the true extent of the west African country’s worrisome budgetary situation.

As a result, the IMF suspended a $1.8-billion aid programme it had agreed upon in 2023, pending further information and commitments from new President Bassirou Diomaye Faye’s government.

The new 36-month arrangement is meant to support Senegal’s “economic and financial reform program for the 2026–2029 period”.

But given past underreporting, it will also require “decisive corrective measures to support the authorities’ request for a waiver regarding the misreporting of data”, the IMF said in a statement.

The staff-level agreement will still need to be approved by the IMF’s executive board.

After the budget scandal erupted in 2024, the IMF found Senegal’s 2023 budget deficit was 12.3 percent of GDP, when the last government had said it was 4.9 percent.

After several IMF visits to Senegal to examine the country’s financial situation, the IMF and the government began negotiations in mid-October for a new aid programme.

Mercedes Vera Martin, division chief at the IMF African Department, told AFP in an interview Tuesday that “since the misreporting was identified, the authorities have taken efforts to improve the transparency.”

“That includes several audits. They have now reconciled their historical data, and recently they published a revised bulletin with the historical data, incorporating the findings of the debt,” she said.

The IMF said in its statement that it would also require “receipt of the necessary financing assurances from Senegal’s partners”.

– Heavily indebted –

With a total public-sector debt estimated at 132 percent of GDP at the end of 2024, according to the IMF, Senegal is one of the most indebted countries in sub-Saharan Africa.

However, its overall fiscal deficit narrowed sharply from 13.4 percent of GDP in 2024 to 6.4 percent of GDP in 2025, mostly driven by spending rationalisation, the IMF said in June.

Senegal has been able to continue financing itself largely through the regional bond market, but this comes at higher costs than loans from international financial institutions, development banks or governments, according to global ratings agency S&P.

Faye became embroiled in a political feud with his then prime minister, Ousmane Sonko, earlier this year over a variety of topics, including the IMF programme.

Although the president sacked Sonko in May, Sonko was afterwards elected as speaker of the National Assembly — a role that could complicate Faye’s ability to usher in IMF reforms.

While Faye prefers a more conciliatory approach with the IMF, Sonko has rejected any debt restructuring.

Asked whether the deal calls for restructuring, Martin said that it included “debt treatment”.

“It’s a sovereign decision. The authorities have a debt treatment plan that will allow us to move forward in our engagement”, Martin said.

Global ratings agency Moody’s last week downgraded Senegal’s long-term foreign-currency debt rating to Caa2 from Caa1, mid-negotiations with the IMF.

That said, “the Senegalese economy has remained resilient, recording 6.7 percent growth in 2025 driven by the first full year of oil production, although non-hydrocarbon GDP growth slowed to 2.2 percent”, Martin said in the IMF’s statement.

Senegal launched production at its first offshore oil field in 2024.

World.title: Car bomb at Colombian police station kills one, injures 11
World.content:
Los Patios – Colombian authorities said Tuesday that a deadly car bombing outside a police station in a northeastern province was carried out by the country’s largest active armed group, weeks after the government launched a new offensive against guerrillas.

The attack on Monday in the department of Norte de Santander killed one civilian and injured eleven others, including two police officers, local officials said.

It came shortly after President Abelardo de la Espriella’s hard-right administration conducted an airstrike against guerrillas in the southern Amazonian department of Guaviare, killing 20 people.

At around midnight, a stolen vehicle loaded with around 80 kilograms of explosives blew up next to the police station in the town of Los Patios, which borders Venezuela.

Local police commander Colonel Jimmy Belalcazar identified the victim as a 23-year-old Venezuelan man.

One of the wounded officers needed to have part of his leg amputated, Belalcazar told Caracol Radio, attributing the bomb to the National Liberation Army (ELN).

Next to the damaged station, dozens of onlookers stared at the flames roaring from the vehicle amid shards of glass and rubble, AFP journalists observed.

Colombia is the world’s largest cocaine producer and is grappling with its worst violence in a decade.

De la Espriella tapped into security fears to win presidential elections in June, although he only won the ballot by less than a percentage point.

He has pledged to get tough on crime by drawing on military support from the United States and Israel to conduct bombing campaigns against guerrillas on Colombian soil.

Monday’s earlier attack in Guaviare was the deadliest military campaign against armed groups in years and followed two more lethal airstrikes earlier in August.

A source at the forensics authority told AFP on Monday that four minors were among the dead in an airstrike last week.

Rights groups warn that children and teens are increasingly being recruited by these groups through slick social media campaigns.

De la Espriella’s leftist predecessor Gustavo Petro tried and failed to negotiate peace with guerrillas including the ELN as well as dissident factions of the rebel army FARC which disbanded in 2016.

Analysts say armed groups used government talks as cover to grow in strength.

Under De la Espriella, Colombia has joined US President Donald Trump’s anti-cartel coalition known as Shield of the Americas.

The Washington-led alliance includes Latin American countries such as Argentina, Ecuador, and El Salvador.

World.title: PetroChina’s production in Iraq drop during first half of 2026
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – PetroChina, China’s largest oil and gas producer, reported a drop in oil production in Iraq during the first half of 2026 because regional conflicts forced temporary closure of plants.

The Chinese firm’s total crude oil output fell 2.8 percent to 462.9 million barrels in the first half of 2026, driven primarily by a 14.2 percent drop in overseas production.

Following the onset of the US-Iran geopolitical crisis, forced project shutdowns and operational disruptions at the company’s main Middle Eastern oilfields, particularly in Iraq, resulted in this rare supply contraction.

Despite the fall in output, the energy giant had a highly profitable first half. Net profit increased 22 percent on an annual basis to 103.94 billion yuan ($14.65 billion), surpassing the 100 billion yuan mark in a half-year period for the first time.

PetroChina executive director Ren Lixin said that Middle Eastern projects are gradually restarting, with regional output returning to over 90 percent of pre-conflict levels, according to South China Morning Post.

The Chinese company has major stakes in some of the world’s largest oil fields, especially in southern and southeastern Iraq.

PetroChina’s biggest projects in Iraq include the West Qurna-1 oil field, Halfaya oil field, Rumaila oil field, and al-Ahdab oil field.

World.title: Iran president urges return to truce, hails Russian support
World.content:
Bishkek – Iran’s President Masoud Pezeshkian on Tuesday vowed to match any US move to return to a June deal aimed at ending their war, warning that diplomatic efforts could be endangered by “pressure and threats” from Washington.

He also thanked Russian leader Vladimir Putin for Moscow’s stance on the conflict, in comments during an international summit in the Kyrgyz capital Bishkek.

Russia and Iran — two of the most sanctioned countries in the world — have massively deepened their military and trade ties during Moscow’s invasion of Ukraine.

Putin and Pezeshkian held talks on the sidelines of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) summit, attended by over a dozen leaders including China’s Xi Jinping and Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi.

They met a day after US President Donald Trump — who has warned Moscow and Beijing against arming Tehran — threatened to hit Iran “hard” after it and the United States traded fire for the first time in weeks.

Pezeshkian told the summit that if the United States returns to the deal aimed at ending months of hostilities, Iran “will immediately take reciprocal action”, according to the Iranian presidency’s website.

The deal, meant to set the stage for final peace talks, has collapsed as both sides accused each other of violating its terms.

Pezeshkian warned Tuesday that a return by the United States to “a policy of pressure and threats could derail the path of diplomacy”.

He later met Putin, telling him: “We appreciate and thank you for your positions at every stage.”

He added: “This shows that our relationship is a strategic relationship; it is not an ordinary relationship.”

– Putin hails Iran’s ‘courage’ –

Putin said that Russia was “trying to provide you with the assistance you need”.

“We admire your courage and resilience in the fight for your national interests,” the Russian leader said, according to Russian media.

“Despite the military and political situation, we are maintaining the momentum of our trade and economic relations from last year,” he added.

Russia and Iran are both under massive international sanctions and have become increasingly reliant on each other.

The US on Monday vowed to keep up a pressure campaign aimed at crippling Tehran’s economy.

The Middle East war began in late February with the US and Israeli attacks on Iran that killed its former supreme leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei.

Iran and the United States resumed exchanging fire on Monday following more than a month of relative calm, with the Strait of Hormuz a key flashpoint.

Tehran has maintained its closure of the strategic waterway, while saying it would return to its commitments under the June deal, which included reopening Hormuz, if the United States did the same.

– ‘A multipolar world’ –

The SCO summit takes place four-and-a-half years into Moscow’s invasion of Ukraine and six months into the war between Washington and Tehran.

The Ukrainian conflict was not mentioned publicly at any point but Putin spoke for an hour and a half with his Turkish counterpart Recep Tayyip Erdogan, whose country has hosted several rounds of talks to put an end to the war, according to the Russian news agency Ria Novosti.

Xi said Russian-Chinese ties had become “more solid” and that their “prospects will be even brighter”, while Putin said cooperation was “successfully developing on all fronts”.

Russia’s economy has become increasingly dependent on China since its full-scale invasion of Ukraine.

The SCO has historically focused on economic issues but has gained momentum in other fields in recent years under Moscow’s and Beijing’s leadership.

“The UN Charter must continue to serve as a key source of international law,” Putin told the summit on Tuesday.

But he added: “It is clear that new multilateral regional structures… are organically integrating into the architecture of a multipolar world alongside the United Nations.”

On top of its 10 members, the SCO now has 15 so-called “dialogue partners”, including Turkey, Saudi Arabia and Qatar, and two observer countries: Afghanistan and Mongolia.

World.title: Safai Karmachari Andolan counters govt reply in Parliament, claims manual scavenging still exists in atleast 46 districts
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Challenging the Centreâs claim made in Parliament in the monsoon session that a survey conducted in all districts of the country during the year 2024-25 found no person engaged as a manual scavenger, Safai Karmachari Andolan (SKA) on Tuesday brought together women from Uttar Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, Bihar and youth from Jammu & Kashmir claiming to be engaged in manual cleaning of human excreta in insanitary latrines to highlight that the illegal practice still persists in atleast 46 districts of these four states.

National Convenor and co-founder of SKA, Bezwada Wilson said that they have evidence by way of photographs showing women lifting waste from dry latrines in these districts. âWe will be writing to the ministry of social justice and empowerment to seek a fresh survey citing this evidence and demand action to stop the illegal practice in these districts within 60 days,â Wilson said.

He, however, made it clear that if the ministry fails to act over the next two months, SKA teams will carry out a survey and put together a report by early next year.

âWe will highlight the findings across states and share them with Parliamentarians and the Judiciary to seek enforcement,â Wilson said.

Former Supreme Court Judges Justice Madan Lokur and Justice Sudhandhu Dhulia and former Patna High Court Judge Justice Anjana Prakash expressed solidarity with the women and men who came forward to share heartwrenching experiences of a life marked by exploitation and untouchability despite the law in place wherein manual scavenging is illegal and dry latrines are banned.





At the meeting held at Press Club of India as SKA announced the launch of a year long campaign âINDIA @ 80â to free the country from manual scavenging, the former judges announced full support. Elaborating on the struggle by those involved in manual scavenging to break free, Justice Lokur expressed concern over the practice persisting despite the protection guaranteed by the Constitution of India against untouchability which is abolished and forbidden.

He also dwelled on the long and continuing struggle for justice by those affected and how they have repeatedly ended up approaching the judiciary that has resulted in various directions from the Supreme Court from time to time. Justice Lokur highlighted that what is most worrying is the denial by authorities that the problem exists and the approach towards addressing the issue shows that ending the problem of manual scavenging is not a priority of the govt.

He asserted that the govt must give priority to remove dry latrines wherever they remain. This he said should be a key focus area under the Swachh Bharat Mission.

Justice Dhulia expressed shock that manual scavenging and dry latrines still exist in more than 40 districts and said that everyone must feel shame that such a practice continues to exist in our society.

Justice Anjana Prakash too expressed concern over the lack of required efforts to end manual scavenging.

As the workers shared their lived experiences as manual scavengers, one heard 71 - year - old Mussi Devi from Sitapur district in UP tell how her entire life has passed cleaning dry latrines and even now she is called by families in her area to manually clean-up and dispose of the waste. âWhen are we going to get freedom from this untouchability?,â asked Mussi Devi and others in her position. Ageing and frail, Devi is also the caregiver for her husband who is paralysed.

35 - year - old Muzzafar Ahmed Sheikh from Jammu and Kashmir shared that he is the third generation in his family engaged in manual scavenging in dry latrines. He shared that his community is subjected to untouchability and even their houses are located in a separate cluster. He hails from Wussan village of Ganderbal. A father of a six - year - old, he says, âI want to break free from this identity of being a manual scavenger and I donât want my son to grow up to do this ever.

â

Bezwada Wilson summed up the sentiment of all those seeking justice. âI started the fight when I was 16 and now I am 60. Many things have changed but manual scavenging in dry latrines still remains. We have to end this menace without fail,â he asserted.

It is pertinent to point that in the monsoon session of Parliament that concluded in August, in response to a written question in Lok Sabha by Leader of Opposition Rahul Gandhi, the minister of state for social justice and empowerment Ramdas Athawale said that as per the "Prohibition of Employment as Manual Scavengers and their Rehabilitation Act, 2013 (MS Act, 2013)", a fresh survey has been conducted in all districts of the country during the year 2024-25 in which no manual scavenger has been found.

âAll the districts of the country have completed the survey and declared themselves as manual scavengers' free,â he said.

However, he also added that 58,098 Manual Scavengers (MS) have been identified during two earlier surveys conducted in 2013 and 2018.

Clearly differentiating "manual scavenging" and "hazardous cleaning", the minister shared while the later pertains to manual cleaning of a sewer or septic tank, without the employer providing protective gear, cleaning devices and safety precautions, a manual scavenger is defined as someone employed for manually cleaning, carrying, disposing of human excreta in an insanitary latrine.

World.title: AIMPLB to launch campaign for protection Constitution and Sharia
World.content:
The All India Muslim Personal Law Board will launch a movement on Sept 17

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The All India Muslim Personal Law Board will launch a movement on Sept 17 to mobilise public opinion for protection of the Constitution and 'Sharia', religious freedom and rights and dignity of citizens. The Board plans to start the campaign from Jantar Mantar in Delhi and reach out to all faiths over three months.In a statement, the board said that as part of the campaign, a charter of demands will be submitted to the President of India Droupadi Murmu through governors in each state. Besides these issues, the charter will also include demands concerning elimination of hate crimes, prevention of unlawful demolitions, protection of Waqf properties and religious places, and equal enforcement of the law.The Board also proposes to bring out a âWhite Paperâ documenting incidents involving discrimination against Muslims, constitutional and human rights violations and release a comprehensive declaration on the issue of lynching.It said over the past several years conditions have emerged wherein vulnerable and marginalised sections, particularly Muslims, have been subjected to discriminatory treatment.The Board listed concerns ranging from extra-legal bulldozer demolitions, attempts to undermine Muslim Personal Law through Uniform Civil Code to undermining the beliefs of the minority community by making the singing of all six verses of Vande Mataram compulsory, as serious challenges to the Constitution of India, social harmony and national unity.Meanwhile, on the controversy following Keralaâs grand mufti Sheikh Abubakr Ahmadâs comments that women should remain confined to their homes and should not enter the public sphere, arguing that Islam prescribed the purdah system to protect their dignity, AIMPLB spokesperson SQR Ilyas objected to the remarks.Noting that Islam nowhere calls for women to be kept confined to the House for their safety, Ilyas said that the interpretation made by Ahmad is ânot correctâ and is therefore âmisplaced.âHe also cited the boardâs profile highlighting that there were nearly 30 women in the AIMPLB and asserted that the board was fully in support of the idea of enabling Muslim women to progress which is in keeping with the Islamic teachings.

World.title: SC: Why not use 'totaliser' to mix votes?
World.content:
NEW DELHI:

Tuesday sought Centre's response to the use of a 'totaliser' mechanism to mix votes from different EVMs before counting, to prevent any backlash from candidates by preserving voter anonymity.

Petitioner advocate Ashwini Upadhyay said a totalisation system hides booth-wise voting patterns by mixing up votes from multiple electronic voting machines (typically around 14) before displaying the count, which helps protect voters from post-poll violence and political victimisation.

, through senior advocate D Seshadri Naidu, said the issue was referred by EC to govt, which consulted stakeholders and found it inadvisable to employ the 'totalisation' mechanism, mainly because of staunch opposition by political parties.

He said a switch to this method would require changing the statute which the commission could not bring about.

When Upadhyay pointed out that the totalisation mechanism was adopted by EC to count paper ballots, a bench of CJI Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana asked Centre to respond on why the same mechanism could not be adopted for EVMs. Upadhyay also said in Jan 2018, EC itself had told the court that the "time had come" to introduce the totaliser to "protect secrecy of the ballot and privacy of the individual".

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines





It had said that "the right of the people staying in a particular locality should not be exposed, and any kind of prejudice or discrimination because of the voting pattern should be avoided".

In a U-turn, EC in its affidavit filed on Aug 31 said, "Experience of litigations has revealed that the present system which includes a simultaneous audit by the candidates is necessary to ensure that frivolous and baseless allegations do not cloud the outcome..." It said the introduction of the totaliser system would give fresh anxieties, misgivings and allegations regarding data, machine tampering and transmission glitches.

World.title: Barefoot mom in sari runs 3km to win Rs 5k for kids' education
World.content:
PUNE: Ramabai Ranvir had no idea what running a race meant. All she had heard was there was Rs 3,000 to be won if she finished first.

So, the 47-year-old widow hopped onto the pickup with a group of police aspirants from the Beed academy where she worked, hoping to compete in what would be the first race of her life.

It didn't bother her that she hadn't trained for the rigours of a long-distance run. It hardly mattered that she was the lone runner without shoes.

In her sari, barefoot after her slippers gave up midway through the run, Ramabai ran 3km with the indomitable spirit of a mother competing for a cash prize that would ease her struggle to pay for her daughters' education, repo-rts Ardhra Nair.

"I ran like my life depended on it. I didn't know how much time I needed to cover the distance.

I only sto-pped once I was past the finish line," she told TOI. "I am so happy they gave me Rs 5,000 instead of Rs 3,000. I bought notebooks and pens for my daughter Pooja. The remaining money is for Arti."

Ramabai works in the kitchen at Dnyandeep Acad-emy, making over 200 chapatis a day for a monthly salary of Rs 9,000.

The native of Potra, Hingoli, took the job to fund the education of her two daughters after her husband died in 2012.





On Aug 28, her younger daughter Arti (20), a BSc computer science student who lives alone in Nanded, called asking for money for food and rent. Ramabai, who didn't have any cash to spare, had a sleepless night.

At dawn, she heard the academy's trainers rounding up aspirants for a running competition nearby. She instantly decided to join in.

"There is no pain worse than that of not being able to take care of your children.

The moment I came to know of the race, winning was the only thing on my mind."

Datta Darade, who heads the academy, said Ramabai's determination moved him. The academy had enrolled her elder daughter Pooja (22) free of cost and given her employment and a room to stay in. "I was taking my students to the marathon. When Ramabai said she wanted to come along, I asked her, 'What will you do there?' She said, 'I will run.' I couldn't believe it when she won in the above-30 category."

Pooja finished second in the 18-30 age group and won Rs 2,000. Arti said she was dumbstruck when her sister called to say their mother had won.

"Our mother studied till Class 7 and has worked all her life, not taking breaks even when she was unwell. She didn't hesitate to send me to Nanded for my studies. I am not surprised she decided to win a race for her family," she said.

World.title: PM Modi repeats call to 'shun unnecessary gold buys, foreign weddings & holidays'
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Buoyed by the better-than-expected GDP growth, PM Modi on Tuesday lauded Indian economy's resilience during a period of global crises. He again pushed for swadeshi goods and urged citizens to shun overseas weddings, foreign vacations and avoid unnecessary gold purchases at a time when imports remain elevated due to high commodity prices in the wake of the West Asia conflict.

His appeal against buying gold also puts to rest speculation around import duties being reviewed by govt. In fact, Centre and RBI are keeping a close watch on shipments. Since Jan, both quantity of gold and value of imports have increased. Since Modi's first appeal in May, however, there has been a drop in quantity of imports but the value of imports is rising due to higher prices, albeit at a slower pace. At $3.5 a kg, the unit value of gold was 94% higher in June, but prices have moderated to $2.8 a kg, which was 47% more than a year ago.

Since Modiâs first appeal in May, gold import quantity has dropped, but import value is rising due to higher prices, albeit slower. Prices moderated to $2.8 a kg, 47% more than a year ago.

While gold remains an investment option for households, higher prices have deterred consumers from buying large quantities, with recycling of old jewellery also rising, industry executives said.

Modi also mounted a withering attack on LoP Rahul Gandhi for spreading pessimism about growth, dismissing his criticism as âjhooth ki goonjâ.





This was Modiâs second reaction to the growth rate within 24 hours. His message mixed praise for peopleâs hard work with disdain for critics like Rahul and reiterated his call to citizens to avoid non-essential gold purchases and foreign trips.

âWe have to maintain this pace and keep growing and, for this,

is essential,â he said in a selfie-video posted on Instagram.

GDP grew at 7.8% in the April-June quarter, bringing relief to the NDA govt, which has been buffeted by the opposition parties, especially Congress under Rahul, over alleged misgovernance.

Modi said, âThere are people within India who are mired in despair, âjhooth ki goonjâ, and are busy spreading pessimism everywhere.â

Emphasising Indiaâs feat, Modi said it came amid global conflicts and crises, causing supply-chain disruption. Since Covid in 2020, stability has remained elusive for the world but India is progressing at a fast pace, he added.

Opposition has a right to criticise govt but especially Congress shouldnât insult people by being incorrigible naysayers and call India a dead economy when data speaks otherwise, finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman said.

BJP played up Rahulâs dismissive comments about the economy to contrast them with Indiaâs growth. Besides his dead economy jibe, Rahul claimed a crisis unseen in peopleâs lifetime would hit the economy. An economic tsunami was coming, he had said. Modi said his govtâs policy is right and intentions clear, calling upon people to work hard. Indiaâs collective strength will take it to new heights. By emphasising swadeshi and self-reliance, people will bequeath a developed India to the young generation.

World.title: Pak takes SCO chair, PM Modi slams use of terror as strategic asset
World.content:
Framing security as a non-negotiable prerequisite for regional progress, PM Narendra Modi delivered a thinly veiled warning to Pakistan over state-sponsored terrorism at the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) summit.

With Pakistan PM Shehbaz Sharif in attendance, Modi said countries that use terrorism as an instrument of state policy, and provide shelter and support to terrorists, must be sent a strong message that terrorism can never be a strategic asset for anyone.

The remarks are significant also because of the timing. Pakistan assumed rotating chairmanship of SCO from Kyrgyzstan on Tuesday and will host the heads-of-state summit next year, for which it will invite Modi, along with others.

Modi made the remarks, in which he also warned against double standards on terrorism, while expanding on India's SCO vision - Security, Connectivity and Opportunity - that he articulated in Tianjin last year.

With Chinese President Xi Jinping also present, PM reiterated India's position that all connectivity initiatives must respect sovereignty and territorial integrity of all states as this is also the "fundamental spirit" of SCO charter.





Modi said that terrorism continued to pose a serious challenge to humanity and it's important to not remain confined to an action-reaction approach in the fight against the menace.

âWe must dismantle the entire ecosystem of terrorist financing, recruitment, radicalisation, and safe havens. We must speak with one voice and make it clear that there can be no place for double standards on this serious issue,â said PM, without naming Pakistan as SCO charter doesnât allow members to raise bilateral differences.

India and Pakistan together joined the China-dominated Eurasian grouping as full members in 2017. For India, the security-oriented SCO has served as a platform not just to assert its strategic autonomy but also flag regional risks from state-sponsored terrorism. Modi said that the blocâs shared aspiration for a peaceful and secure Eurasia is also closely linked to peace and stability in Afghanistan and that India will continue to contribute to the development and provision of humanitarian assistance to people of the country.

Modi addressed West Asia crisis, saying it was affecting energy security, maritime trade and supply chains around the world and recalling his message earlier that conflicts cannot be resolved on the battlefield. âCountries of Global South bear greatest brunt of such disruptions. Therefore, India has consistently called for all tensions and conflicts to be resolved not on battlefield, but through dialogue and diplomacy,â he added.

While underlining the importance India attaches to SCO, Modi said that at a time when the world is passing through instability, the organisation must transform the shared geography into opportunities and bring about positive change in peopleâs lives. Describing SCO as a confluence of great civilisations, cultures, and ideas, he said that over next 25 years, people-to-people ties should remain at the heart of cooperation among the member states.

âTrue measure of our success should be how many new opportunities our efforts create, how many new markets open up for entrepreneurs, how much farmers benefit from tech, and how much better the lives of our citizens become,â said the PM. According to an Indian readout of PMâs participation, Modi stated that strong and trusted connectivity initiatives were important for the groupâs shared progress and prosperity.

World.title: SC orders extradition of crypto accused
World.content:
SC has directed Centre, CBI and Himachal govt to bring Subhash Sharma to justice by getting him extradited

NEW DELHI: Taking note that the main accused in Rs 20,000 crore cryptocurrency fraud case is safely holed up in Dubai for more than a year after duping around 2.5 lakh investors, SC has directed Centre, CBI and Himachal govt to bring Subhash Sharma to justice by getting him extradited. A bench of Justices J B Pardiwala and K Vinod Chandran also directed attachment of all movable and immovable property of Sharma and his relatives.An FIR was registered in the case in 2023 and Sharma fled the country but the other accused were arrested in 2025.Granting bail to one of the accused in the case, the bench passed the order to extradite Sharma. It also requested Chief Justice of HP HC to constitute a special court to exclusively deal with this crime.

World.title: Tribunal alters gay ex-IAF man 'dismissal' to 'routine discharge'
World.content:
Instead of granting the discharge, IAF initiated a court of inquiry

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The principal bench of Armed Forces Tribunal (AFT) has converted the order of dismissal of a non-commissioned IAF officer, who confessed to being gay, into a routine discharge.The bench, headed by Justice Rajendra Menon and Justice Rasika Chaube, ruled that substituting dismissal with routine discharge prevents lasting career stigma for the ex-officer seeking employment outside the armed forces.The non-commissioned IAF officer, who had served about 10 and a half years, had applied for a compassionate premature discharge in 2024 to settle down with his partner, disclosing his relationship in an application.Instead of granting the discharge, IAF initiated a court of inquiry. The inquiry concluded he had breached discipline and risked national security by entering into a relationship with a foreigner. The court of inquiry also found him guilty of travelling abroad (Thailand and Sri Lanka) without permission. He was subsequently dismissed from service earlier this year.He then approached AFT principal bench not to challenge IAF's disciplinary right, but to request "dismissal" be changed to a "discharge" so he could seek future civilian employment.The bench held that while dismissal is warranted when rules are breached, exceptions must be considered in this case. "The respondents could have granted discharge to the applicant, but in the garb of maintaining discipline they dismissed him. The effect of both is identical inasmuch as the respondents do not want the service of the applicant."

World.title: Pink tickets to continue till Sept. 17; Saheli cards mandatory thereafter, say officials
World.content:
The Delhi Transport Department has announced September 17 as the last day for women commuters to avail of free travel on DTC and cluster buses using the ‘pink tickets’ system. After this, the scheme will not be extended, an official said.

Delhi women will need a Pink Saheli National Common Mobility Card (NCMC) from September 18 onward to travel for free while non-resident women will have to pay for tickets.

The NCMC cards were launched on March 2 to enable paperless, free travel for women in Delhi, replacing the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) government’s ‘pink tickets’ scheme.

Chief Minister Rekha Gupta has alleged that the AAP-era scheme has been “marred by corruption and that the panic buttons were installed just for show”.

‘Great enthusiasm’

“Women of Delhi have shown tremendous enthusiasm for the Pink Saheli Smart Card. Around 19 lakh women have already applied or registered for the card,” said Transport Minister Pankaj Kumar Singh.

The government has also reduced the number of distribution centres where these cards could be issued from 73 to 38. The number had been increased from 50 at the time of the scheme’s launch to 73.

Upcoming festivals

The deadline falls during the period marked by several festivals, including Janmashtami, Teej and Ganesh Chaturthi, when women travel for religious, cultural and social events.

World.title: 66% names dropped from Delhi draft roll marked ‘shifted’
World.content:
More than six in every 10 names left out of Delhi’s draft roll published on Monday are marked ‘permanently shifted’ and account for the largest share of the 47.56 lakh exclusions in the ongoing special intensive revision (SIR) drive.

Of the entries removed at the draft stage, 31.59 lakh are marked ‘permanently shifted’, 11.73 lakh ‘untraceable/absent’, 2.82 lakh ‘dead’ and 1.41 lakh ‘duplicate’ or ‘already enrolled’. Over 10 lakh of those marked ‘permanently shifted’ are aged 30-39.

The excluded entries have been placed in four categories — ‘absent’, ‘shifted’, ‘dead’ and ‘duplicate’ (ASDD). Analysis of the list of ASDD voters across all 14,947 polling booths, uploaded on the Delhi Chief Electoral Officer (CEO) website, shows that in at least one booth in each of the 70 Assembly constituencies, over 95% of the names were placed in one of the four categories.

In 1,042 of the 1,090 booths where at least 95% of the removals were attributed to a single reason, ‘permanently shifted’ was the reason. These 1,042 booths together account for nearly 4.5 lakh deletions, of which 4.37 lakh were classified as ‘permanently shifted’. Most of these booths — where at least 95% of the excluded names are marked ‘permanently shifted’ — are in South East (216) and South (204) districts, with North East at the third spot (147).

Most such booths are in Deoli, Tughlaqabad, Okhla, Karawal Nagar, Kasturba Nagar and Mustafabad.

Single-reason pattern

Nearly half of the 1,090 booths with such a highly concentrated single-reason pattern were located near another booth with the same pattern.

In two polling booths in Shyam Nagar under the Rajouri Garden constituency, all 617 removed names were marked as ‘absent/ untraceable’.

Of 2.82 lakh entries marked ‘dead’, 22,918 electors are below 40 years of age. Among electors aged 85 and above who were subjected to additional verification during enumeration, around 49,700 (54.9%) are on the ASDD list. Of these, the majority are marked as permanently shifted or absent.

The exclusions can be challenged during the claims and objections period, which ends on September 30.

Delhi CEO Ashok Kumar on Monday said voters whose names are missing can submit Form 6 for inclusion. He said no name will be removed from the final roll without proper inquiry and notice.

Booth-level agents can assist electors in filing claims, subject to a limit of 40 forms per agent, an official said, adding that special camps will be organised for the process.

A senior poll official said their office expects around half of those marked as permanently shifted to be restored to the rolls during the claims and objections process.

World.title: U.S. strikes Iran and Tehran fires back as hostilities flare again
World.content:
The U.S. military hit targets in Iran on Tuesday (September 1, 2026), and Tehran fired missiles and drones in response as hostilities flare once again in an intermittent war that has lasted more than six months.

The U.S. strikes followed others on Sunday that abruptly ended a month without military action and threatened to fully reignite a conflict that has spiked global oil prices and posed political problems for Republicans in November’s midterm congressional elections. The renewed fighting comes after President Donald Trump had appeared to pivot toward trying to bend Iran to his will through economic sanctions.

“If the failed Nation of Iran retaliates for this very justified attack, they will be hit again at a much harder and higher level, but it will not be the biggest attack of them all, that is waiting in the wings,” Mr. Trump warned on social media.

Today at 12 p.m. ET, U.S. forces began striking Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) targets in Iran. The strikes follow recent attempted attacks by the IRGC against commercial shipping in the Strait of Hormuz and against American service members deployed to the region. — U.S. Central Command (@CENTCOM) September 1, 2026

U.S. Central Command said the latest strikes were in response to Tehran trying to attack commercial ships and American forces in the Middle East. Trump offered an additional explanation, telling Fox News in a phone call that U.S. forces struck Iran’s radars.

“They tried to rebuild their radar because they can’t see anything,” Mr. Trump told Fox. “We waited until it was almost built and then we hit it.”

Iranian state media reported that the U.S. had bombed civilian sites along Iran’s southern coast and hit a civilian airport. A U.S. strike hit a home where a wedding ceremony was being held in Kuhestak in southern Iran, killing two people and wounding at least 20 others, Ahmad Nafisi, Hormozgan Province’s deputy governor, told Iranian state television in a phone call.

Iran’s Armed Forces General Staff and its joint military command said the armed forces would deliver what they described as “crushing and devastating blows” against the United States. The state-run IRNA news agency cited a statement by Iran’s paramilitary Revolutionary Guard, which warned that the attacks have only strengthened the Islamic Republic’s resolve and tightened Iran’s effective closure of the Strait of Hormuz, through which 20% of the world’s oil normally flows.

Explosions were reported across several southern Iranian coastal areas, including the port city of Bandar Abbas that is home to naval and air force facilities as well as Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz. Witnesses in Bandar Abbas told The Associated Press that the explosions were stronger than those on Sunday and said they saw smoke rising from the eastern part of the city on the strait.

Iranian state television said U.S. strikes hit a fishmeal factory on Qeshm Island and several civilian sites in Hormozgan province. It said a fishing pier and a Ports and Maritime Organization tower in Sirik were among the locations struck.

State TV also reported that the U.S. military struck the civilian Jiroft Airport in central Iran’s Kerman province, saying a projectile struck an area outside the runway and caused no casualties or damage to airport infrastructure. U.S. Central Command did not immediately respond to an email seeking comment on those reports.

The U.S. and Iran are both seeking control over the Strait of Hormuz, a narrow waterway off Iran’s coast that is a vital oil shipping corridor. Tehran effectively closed it after the war began.

Oil prices have moved sharply higher this week with renewed clashes between Iran and the United States. Crude, already up about 7% this week, continued to rise following the strikes on Tuesday.

The price of crude has jumped more than 50% this year and it’s dragged the cost of gasoline upward with it. The cost for a gallon of regular gasoline in the U.S. ticked higher again overnight to $4.10, according to AAA. Last year at this time, a gallon cost $3.19.

Before military action began again, the Trump administration had argued that hitting the right economic target in a campaign of financial isolation would get Tehran to its breaking point. Now, strikes are renewing even as U.S. stockpiles of advanced interceptors have been diminishing and the war has been unpopular among many Americans.

A return to open conflict would be dangerous for the region, where Iran has targeted U.S. military bases and infrastructure in Gulf countries since the war began.

Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian said earlier Tuesday before the latest strikes that the Islamic Republic is ready to return to the interim ceasefire deal reached with the U.S. in June if Washington does the same.

“If the U.S. returns to its commitments in the memorandum of understanding, the Islamic Republic of Iran will immediately reciprocate,” Iranian state media cited Pezeshkian as saying at the Shanghai Cooperation Organization summit in Kyrgyzstan.

The June interim deal called for an immediate ceasefire and started a 60-day period for negotiations aimed at reaching a wider agreement, but crumbled soon afterward.

In the previous strikes on Sunday, U.S. Central Command said its forces struck Iranian rocket launchers that would launch sea mines into the strait.

Iran responded to Sunday’s attacks by launching missiles at U.S. sites in Jordan, which were intercepted, while United Arab Emirates said it stopped an Iranian drone over its waters. Trump acknowledged Monday that more strikes might be necessary.

The American military in recent days has cast the renewed fighting as limited, though Trump had acknowledged Monday that more strikes might be necessary.

U.S. Central Command said Monday on X that its attacks on Iranian targets on Sunday were narrowly focused.

“U. S. forces took limited, precise action against IRGC minelaying forces posing an imminent threat in the Strait of Hormuz,” U.S. Central Command said. “In essence, Iran created the threat and the U.S. military eliminated it to protect civilian mariners, commercial shipping, and the free flow of global commerce.”

Central Command reiterated Tuesday that its attacks followed Iranian aggression against commercial vessels and American troops in the region.

World.title: IndiGo flight makes emergency landing in Goa after engine failure
World.content:
A Delhi-bound IndiGo flight with 229 passengers on board returned to Goa about 30 minutes after takeoff on Tuesday (September 1, 2026) and made an emergency landing at Manohar International Airport after one engine failed mid-air, sources said.

The aircraft landed safely at the airport in Mopa, North Goa.

“IndiGo flight 6E 2102, which departed for Delhi at 9.16 a.m., returned to Goa after reporting a failure in one of its engines. The Air Traffic Control declared a full emergency around 9.30 a.m., and the aircraft landed safely on runway 28 at 9.51 a.m.,” a source said.

An IndiGo spokesperson said in a statement that a “technical issue was detected shortly after takeoff”. “Following the standard operating procedure, the relevant authorities were informed, and the pilots turned back and landed the aircraft safely at Manohar International Airport,” the airline said.

The aircraft is currently undergoing maintenance checks and will resume operations after securing all necessary clearances, it said. Arrangements were made for the passengers to reach their destination, the airline added.

World.title: Defence PSUs told to reduce dependence on imports
World.content:
Union Defence Minister Rajnath Singh on Tuesday (September 1, 2026) reviewed the annual performance of all 16 defence Public Sector Undertakings (PSUs).

In a meeting, the Minister called upon the defence PSUs to reduce import dependence, strengthen research and development, ensure timely delivery of major projects, and transform themselves into globally competitive defence companies, the Union Ministry of Defence said in a statement.

Mr. Singh, along with the Minister of State for Defence Sanjay Seth, was briefed by Secretary (Defence Production) Sanjeev Kumar, and the Chairmen and MDs of the defence PSUs on their performance, achievements, and roadmaps, the Ministry said.

Mr. Singh reviewed the progress made by state-owned defence companies in improving indigenous manufacturing capabilities, defence technologies, exports, and supply chains, and executing major projects.

During the meeting, the heads of seven defence PSUs — Hindustan Aeronautics Limited, Mazagon Dock Shipbuilders Limited, Bharat Electronics Limited, Bharat Dynamics Limited, Garden Reach Shipbuilders and Engineers Limited, BEML, and MIDHANI — presented dividend cheques totalling ₹3,951 crore to Mr. Singh towards the government’s equity shares for 2025-26.

Commending the defence PSUs for their contribution in strengthening India’s defence manufacturing ecosystem and advancing the vision of ‘Aatmanirbhar Bharat’, Mr. Singh said their performance reflected the country’s growing capabilities in building a robust indigenous defence industrial base.

India achieved defence production worth approximately ₹1.8 lakh crore during 2025-26, with the 16 defence PSUs contributing ₹1.29 lakh crore, he said, describing the achievement as a significant milestone in the country’s journey towards an aatmanirbhar (self-reliant) defence industrial base.

Mr. Singh urged the defence PSUs to focus on timely delivery of equipment, reducing import dependence, converting R&D investments into technological leadership, increasing defence exports, improving productivity through capital expenditure, and expanding support for start-ups and micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs).

“The progress of defence PSUs is not merely an economic or industrial necessity; it is a national security imperative,” the Minister said, noting that recent global conflicts had demonstrated the importance of assured supply chains, surge production capacity, availability of critical spares, rapid repair capabilities, and the ability to sustain manufacturing during prolonged conflicts.

The success of research and development should not be judged merely by the amount of money spent but by tangible outcomes, including the development of new technologies, intellectual property, prototypes, and operational products, Mr. Singh said.

While welcoming the increasing investment in R&D by the defence PSUs, Mr. Singh said India must identify niche technology areas where it could emerge not only self-reliant but also as a global leader.

He also stressed the need for defence PSUs to elevate product quality to international standards as India seeks to expand its presence in global defence markets.

“In pursuit of the ‘Make in India, Make for the World’ objective, we must resolve to transform all defence PSUs into global giants,” he said.

Mr. Singh also released four publications on self-reliance, indigenisation, innovation, and future defence capabilities.

World.title: Congress attacks BJP over exclusion of over 2 crore voters in Maharashtra SIR
World.content:
Flagging the exclusion of 2.06 crore names in Maharashtra’s draft electoral rolls after the special intensive revision (SIR), the Congress on Tuesday (September 1, 2026) said votes were being added and deleted to ensure that the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) wins elections.

The deletions in Maharashtra, where draft rolls were published on Monday (August 31), are the largest in absolute numbers for any State in the ongoing Phase 3 of the SIR.

Following the 2024 Maharashtra elections, the Congress had formally submitted representations to the Election Commission alleging large-scale voter roll manipulation, including unusual voter spikes in several constituencies. It had alleged that forged documentation, such as fake Aadhaar cards with mismatched names and photos, were used to add fictitious voters without physical verification of addresses.

On Tuesday (September 1, 2026), Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi said “the BJP and the ‘vote theft commission’ keep changing their tactics, and they will continue to do so; the goal remains just one: BJP’s victory at any cost, and the end of India’s democracy”.

In a post on X, he said: “Maharashtra 2024 - Suddenly, 3.9 million new voters were added between the Lok Sabha and Vidhan Sabha elections. I said it then, and I say it today: This was vote theft.”

“And now in Maharashtra, 2.07 crore voters have been removed from the draft list — that’s every fifth voter. Lok Sabha 2024: 9.29 crore, Vidhan Sabha 2024: 9.7 crore, SIR 2026: 7.78 crore. Which list was correct,” Mr. Gandhi asked.

“For a government built on vote theft, the people are not important—that’s why this BJP neither listens to the people nor obeys their command,” he added.

Congress President Mallikarjun Kharge said votes are added when it suits the BJP. “Where it doesn’t, votes are split to perpetrate vote theft,” he said.

“The BJP’s conspiracy to hollow out Indian democracy by stealing votes is coming out into the open. Instead of acting as the guardian of fair elections, the Election Commission is functioning like the “Save BJP’s Chair Commission,” he wrote on X.

Both leaders said that in West Bengal, 91% of the voter names struck off in the SIR had to be reinstated after appeals. “That means 9 out of every 10 names were wrongly deleted, and added back only after the election. I said it then, and I say it today: This was vote theft”, Mr. Gandhi said.

Mr. Kharge said that the “same game” was being repeated in Delhi. “Voters were increased before the Assembly elections, then names of 4.756 million voters vanished from the draft list, and preparations are underway to issue notices to 3.3 million other voters,” he said.

He said that in Telangana and Karnataka, Congress workers faced similar manipulations every day. “The country is now uniting against vote theft. The nation has understood the BJP’s conspiracy, the thief has been caught. Punishment will surely be meted out for holding democracy captive,” he added.

The Election Commission, meanwhile, has shared figures showing that 3,35,910 booth-level agents appointed by different recognised political parties were engaged in preparing the draft electoral roll for Maharashtra, and another 33,226 for Delhi.

World.title: Zelenskyy warns 'safe days in Russian skies are over'
World.content:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy on Tuesday (September 1, 2026) warned airlines, insurance firms and passengers that Russian airspace would be "completely unsafe" and filled with Ukrainian drones for the duration of the war.

“Today, we want to warn every airline that uses Russian airspace, every insurer, and everyone who still uses Russia’s key airports: Russian airspace is becoming completely unsafe,” he said in his nightly address.

“Ukraine does not threaten civilian aviation as such — not a single civilian aircraft. There will simply be drones in Russia’s skies on a scale that has to be taken into account,” he said.

More than four years after the start of Russia’s invasion of Ukraine, both Moscow and Kyiv have intensified their deadly strikes.

At least 12 people were killed on Tuesday (September 1, 2026) in Kyiv and the surrounding region during fresh massive overnight Russian strikes.

Air traffic at Russian airports is also regularly disrupted by the approach of Ukrainian drones, the number of which has increased in recent months.

“We in Ukraine do not want innocent lives to be lost. That is why we are warning our partners: the safe days in Russia’s skies are over,” Mr. Zelenskyy said.

“Drone-infested skies are no place for civilian aviation,” he added. “The sky over Russia is currently for drones... as long as the war continues.”

He said Ukraine would, however, clear its drones from Russian skies when its partners requested it, “for the sake of diplomacy, for the sake of negotiations... for specific periods of time and in specific destinations”.

Diplomatic efforts under U.S. mediation to end the conflict have stalled since the outbreak of war in the West Asia in February.

World.title: India’s ambition will be settled in small enterprises, says SICCI president
World.content:
CHENNAI

The Southern India Chamber of Commerce and Industry (SICCI) continues to play an important role in bringing together industry, government and other stakeholders to address emerging opportunities and challenges for businesses across southern India said its president Arun Alagappan at the chamber’s 116th Annual General Meeting.

“India’s ambition for 2047 will not be settled in its boardrooms. It will be settled in its small enterprises. Whether the priority is manufacturing, agriculture, technology, infrastructure, defence, the green and blue economy or global trade, not one of these can be carried out without the MSME sector,” he said.

Mr. Alagappan further said that the next decade also belongs to the States: Tamil Nadu is building towards a trillion-dollar economy and Andhra Pradesh has set itself an equally serious ambition in Swarnandhra @2047, and in both cases it is the small enterprise, not the large corporation, that will decide whether those targets are met. “Southern India has the industrial base, the ports and the talent to lead that effort. What is needed now is for the government and the industry to move together — enterprise by enterprise, cluster by cluster and district by district,” he noted.

Kondapalli Srinivas, Minister for MSME, SERP, NRI Relations and Empowerment, Government of Andhra Pradesh, in his inaugural address, said that the empowerment of a household is the foundation for building a stronger State and a stronger nation.

“By creating opportunities for entrepreneurship, employment and higher incomes, we can enable households to contribute meaningfully to economic growth. Andhra Pradesh is taking steps to create an enabling ecosystem for MSMEs through industrial parks, common facilities, access to finance and innovation,” he added.

World.title: 5 security personnel among 6 martyred in Balochistan Customs House attack, 21 terrorists killed across province: ISPR
World.content:
Five security personnel, including two officers, and a Customs official were martyred during a “coordinated attack in an attempt to breach the Customs House” on the night of August 31-September 1 in Balochistan, the military’s media wing said.

In a statement issued on Tuesday, Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) said that on the night of Aug 31-Sept 1, during multiple incidents in Nokcha, Chagai District, and Ziarat Cross, Pishin District, twenty-one terrorists belonging to Indian-sponsored proxies of Fitna al-Hindustan and Fitna al-Khawarij were sent to hell due to effective responses by the Security Forces.

The state uses the term Fitna-al-Khawarij for the banned Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan (TTP) and has designated Balochistan-based groups as Fitna-al-Hindustan to highlight India’s alleged role in terrorism and destabilisation across Pakistan.

“During the night of Aug 31-Sep 1, terrorists belonging to Fitna al- Khawarij launched a coordinated attack in an attempt to breach the Customs House.

“Security forces responded effectively and, after an intense fire exchange, killed 10 terrorists,” ISPR added.

Moreover, fleeing terrorists were also engaged by the security forces, inflicting further casualties, the ISPR said.

“During the exchange of fire, six brave sons of the soil, including two officers and a government official from the Customs Department, made the ultimate sacrifice in the line of duty and embraced shahadat,” it said.

The attack on the Customs House was a “manifestation of the terror-crime nexus, orchestrated to prevent Customs officials from performing their lawful duties and thereby facilitate the continuation of criminal activities in the area”, the ISPR stated.

It added that the sanitisation operations were continuing in the surrounding areas to eliminate any remaining terrorists and ensure the safety and security of the local population as well as the vital national highways.

Separately, on 31 August, terrorists belonging to Fitna al-Hindustan attempted to disrupt the peaceful movement of commuters along N-40 Quetta–Taftan Highway by establishing an illegal checkpoint for extortion, ISPR said.

“Security forces responded immediately and, after an intense fire exchange, 11 terrorists were killed on the spot.

“A large quantity of weapons, ammunition and explosives was also recovered from the terrorists,” it added.

“The relentless counter-terrorism campaign under the vision of ‘Azm-i-Istehkam,’ as approved by the Federal Apex Committee on the National Action Plan, will continue with full resolve. Security forces and law enforcement agencies remain committed to eliminating the menace of foreign-sponsored and foreign-supported terrorism from the country,” the ISPR concluded.

On Monday, the security forces killed 12 terrorists following an attack on a convoy of vehicles from the Reko Diq copper and gold project, in the Chagai area.

On the same day, it was reported that two terrorists had also been killed during an intelligence-based operation (IBO) in Washuk district.

World.title: Govt raises petrol price by Rs1.08, high-speed diesel by Rs0.51
World.content:
The government on Tuesday raised the price of petrol by Rs1.08 per litre and that of high-speed diesel (HSD) by Rs0.51 per litre.

Following the revision, petrol will retail at Rs343.87 per litre while HSD will cost Rs370.92 per litre. The government continues to levy Rs114 per litre in taxes and duties on petrol and Rs100 per litre on diesel.

According to the Petroleum Division’s notification, the new prices will be applicable on September 2 (Wednesday).

The price of HSD has come down from a peak of Rs520.35 recorded on April 3. Its price had started rising from Rs281 per litre after the US-Iran war broke out on February 28.

The petrol price had peaked at Rs458.41 on April 3 after beginning its upward trajectory from Rs266 in the first week of March.

On July 17, Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik announced that fuel prices would now be fixed on a daily basis due to fluctuations in international market prices following renewed hostilities between Iran and the US.

Prior to this, the government had been announcing weekly revisions to fuel prices since early March, alongside measures for the conservation of fuel amid possible oil supply disruptions due to the ongoing conflict in the Middle East. The federal government in April also announced targeted relief measures to provide subsidised fuel.

The petroleum minister stated that the cabinet and the prime minister had decided to give the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (Ogra) the responsibility of deciding fuel prices on a daily basis based on international market trends.

Petrol is mainly used in private transport, small vehicles, rickshaws and two-wheelers, and changes in its price affect the middle and lower-middle classes.

Similarly, changes in diesel prices also impact the public at large, as it is mainly used in the heavy transport sector, power plants and large generators.

Petrol and high-speed diesel (HSD) are the major revenue earners, with monthly sales of about 700,000 to 800,000 tonnes, compared to just 10,000 tonnes of monthly demand for kerosene.

World.title: PM Shehbaz says water ‘lifeblood’ of region, must never be weaponised
World.content:
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Tuesday said water was the “lifeblood” of the region and must never be weaponised, as he addressed a summit of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) in Kyrgyzstan.

Speaking at the SCO Council of Heads of States (CHS) meeting in the Kyrgyz capital Bishkek, the premier said the region cannot “realise its full potential without lasting peace”.

Without naming India directly, he highlighted the issue of the Indus Waters Treaty (IWT) and demanded that it be honoured.

“Water is the lifeblood of our region. It sustains millions of lives, nourishes our land and secures the very future of our coming generations,” he noted.

He stressed that it “must never be weaponised; it cannot be used as an instrument of coercion, nor can it ever be exploited for political leverage”.

“The treaties governing our shared waters are solemn, binding international commitments. They are not matters of political convenience to be cast aside at your will. They must be honoured unconditionally, in both letter and spirit.”

In a later statement on X, the premier said he was honoured to address the ceremony as Pakistan assumed chairmanship of the SCO, reiterating that water “is the lifeblood of our region” and must never be weaponised by any state.

He also noted that Pakistan made “immense sacrifices in the fight against terrorism”, and added that Pakistan will conduct its chairmanship of the body under the theme ‘Turning Vision into Action: Connectivity, Innovation and Shared Prosperity’.

“I am confident that the SCO will continue to grow from strength to strength and bring meaningful improvements to the lives of its more than 3 billion people,” he writes.

The prime minister’s speech comes a day after the Permanent Court of Arbitration (PCA) ordered India to uphold the IWT with Pakistan and suspend work on a hydro project in occupied Kashmir.

The Hague-based court backed Pakistan’s stance, declaring that the IWT between the two countries remained fully in force, as India had no justification for ending or suspending the agreement.

Water and the IWT remain a contentious issue between India and Pakistan, following New Delhi’s unilateral abeyance of the accord in April last year — a move that was followed by a brief military conflict between the two sides in May 2025.

‘Terrorism one of the gravest threats’

Speaking on the issue of terrorism, PM Shehbaz said it remained “one of the gravest threats that has affected our entire region in its various forms and manifestations”.

As chair of the SCO Regional Anti-Terrorist Structure (RATS), Pakistan has “worked actively to strengthen regional counter-terrorism cooperation”, he highlighted.

“Few nations have fought against the scourge of terrorism as resolutely and valiantly as Pakistan. In the past two and a half decades, we have sacrificed more than 90,000 lives and endured economic losses of over $150 billion in combatting terrorism.”

Pakistan sought a peaceful and stable Afghanistan, he said, adding: “But let there be no ambiguity; so long as terrorists continue to use Afghan territory to shed the blood of innocent Pakistanis and other nations, lasting peace will remain beyond our reach.”

In his speech, the prime minister also mentioned Pakistan’s mediation efforts in the US-Iran war and laid out the country’s plan as it assumed the SCO CHS chair.

PM Shehbaz was welcomed by the Kyrgyz president upon his arrival at the summit’s venue on Tuesday, and later posed with other world leaders for a group photo.

Leaders from China, Iran, Turkiye, Russia, and India were also in Kyrgyzstan for the two-day summit. The regional bloc, which also includes Kyrgyzstan, Kazakhstan, Tajikistan, Uzbekistan and Belarus, is celebrating its 25th anniversary.

A video clip shared by the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO) showed PM Shehbaz speaking to China’s President Xi Jinping. He could also be seen sitting together with Russian President Vladimir Putin and Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan.

The premier also held informal meetings with the presidents of Iran, Uzbekistan, Kazakhstan, Tajikistan and Belarus.

Taking SCO chair, Pakistan proposes ‘excellent plan’

Pakistan has assumed the chairmanship of the SCO CHS for 2026–27, with next year’s summit to be hosted by Islamabad.

“As Pakistan assumes the chairmanship of the SCO, we are proposing an excellent plan that will prioritise key sectors, including IT and AI, energy development, poverty reduction, disaster management, health, culture and sports,” PM Shehbaz said during his address.

As part of that plan, Pakistan proposed establishing an SCO framework for sovereign AI infrastructure and governance to “promote responsible and inclusive AI development and to also ensure that no member state is left behind”.

The prime minister said Pakistan’s SCO chairmanship will be pursued under the theme, ‘Turning vision into action, connectivity, innovation and shared prosperity’.

“We undertake this responsibility with humility, hope and abiding faith that connectivity will bring our peoples closer, innovation will open new doors of opportunity, and shared prosperity will reach every home,” the premier said.
