Tech.title: Sony Owes Gamers $7.85 Million in PlayStation Store Credit: See if You Qualify
Tech.content:
If you’re a US PlayStation customer, you may be eligible to claim part of a $7.85 million settlement payout. The case focused on an allegation that Sony “unlawfully eliminated competition and monopolized the market for [its] digital games” by discontinuing the sale of game-specific vouchers that let PlayStation owners buy digital games from other online retailers.

The class action lawsuit Caccuri v. Sony Interactive Entertainment alleged that Sony’s actions caused “consumers to pay more for certain digital games than they otherwise would have paid on the PlayStation Store.” It alleges that this action violates antitrust laws because it forces PlayStation customers to buy from a single storefront at an inflated price.

Put simply, the lawsuit alleges that Sony limited the sale of digital games on other marketplaces, funneling customers into its own PlayStation Store. Some of these games include PlayStation exclusives such as The Last of Us, as well as third-party titles like the Mass Effect Trilogy and Resident Evil 4.

The lawsuit was initially settled in 2024, but the settlement was rejected twice during the approval process — most recently in July 2025 (PDF), when the presiding judge said the proposed plan “[did] not provide an estimated recovery or a range of potential recovery for class members.” The approval process was reinitiated in April.

Sony has denied any wrongdoing or that settlement class members were damaged by its actions, and the court has not decided if the company violated any laws. Despite this, the court has preliminarily approved the $7.85 million settlement payment, subject to the court’s final approval hearing.

The settlement website is live now. The hearing is scheduled for Oct. 15, and it’s meant to confirm the settlement amount, allocate up to 25% of the funds for attorneys’ fees, and create a plan to distribute the remainder to eligible class members.

If you fit all of the criteria to be part of the Sony PlayStation game-voucher settlement, you’re automatically a class member in this lawsuit and will be able to collect a portion of the settlement money — added directly to your PlayStation Network account wallet — sometime after the final approval hearing.

Gamers who have deactivated their PlayStation Network accounts can apply for the settlement payment by sending qualifying purchase information to the email address info@PSNDigitalGamesSettlement.com. Customers with deactivated accounts will receive cash payments instead of PSN account accreditation.

The option to opt out of the settlement to retain your right to sue Sony separately in regard to its game-voucher sales practices closed on July 2. A written request to the court opting out of or objecting to the settlement had to be received by then; otherwise, you will remain part of the settlement class.

Who can be part of the Sony PlayStation settlement?

Not every PlayStation owner is automatically eligible. The money is reserved for those who purchased a digital game through the PlayStation Store after Sony ceased selling game-specific vouchers for alternative online storefronts.

In order to join, you must meet the following qualifications:

Be a living individual human being in the US or its territories. Have purchased one of the eligible digital games (PDF) through the PlayStation Store between the period of April 1, 2019, and Dec. 31, 2023.

Affected individuals are automatically part of the settlement class and will receive their compensation through their PlayStation Network account wallet, subject to approval at the final hearing, the date and time of which could change. Any updates will be posted to the settlement website.

How much will the Sony PlayStation settlement pay?

It’s unclear how much each settlement class member will receive, though we know affected parties will automatically receive compensation in the form of PlayStation account funds.

Up to a quarter of the $7.85 million settlement will be used to pay attorneys’ fees, taxes and other administrative costs. The remaining settlement money will be administered equally to every settlement class member. Settlement class members will likely see a couple of dollars added to their PlayStation accounts once the funds are fully allocated.

Tech.title: Firefox Now Lets You Block Some Ads on iOS Devices
Tech.content:
Fewer ads, better browsing? Firefox has added a new feature called Ad Blocker for Firefox on iOS, which the company says will block many third-party ads and ad-related trackers when you use the browser on iPhones, iPads and other iOS devices.

Ad Blocker is turned off by default, but you can enable it in Settings > Browsing > Ad Blocker. If you get ads that should have been blocked or other oddities while using the new feature, go to this Mozilla Connect page to report them.

A representative for Mozilla told CNET that Ad Blocker will work on iPhones running iOS 15 or later and on iPads running iPadOS 15 or later. The feature is being rolled out progressively, so some people may not see it right away.

Firefox, owned by Mozilla, is a web browser launched in 2004. Though it’s less popular than other browsers like Google Chrome, Apple Safari and Microsoft Edge, Firefox fans cite privacy protections and customizations as some of the main reasons they like the browser.

Other niche browsers also block ads, including Brave, Opera, Vivaldi, Avast and DuckDuckGo. If you use Chrome or Edge, you can install extensions such as uBlock Origin or AdGuard from their respective stores.

“Advertising helps fund much of the open web, supporting the publishers, creators and websites people rely on,” Mozilla said in its announcement. “We also know that ads can sometimes crowd the screen or interrupt what you’re trying to do.”

What it does, what it can’t

When you’re checking out a web page, it can be fairly annoying when pop-up ads and overlays cover up content you’re trying to see. Mozilla says Ad Blocker can stop many of those before they load, reducing clutter on that particular page.

Mozilla says the Ad Blocker tech uses Apple’s WebKit Content Blocker technology and EasyList, a filter list used by browsers and ad-blocking extensions, to determine which ads to block.

Even with the new tool, you’ll still see ads here and there. For example, if you search “best air conditioners” on Google, merchant ads for AC units are likely to appear somewhere on that Google page. Ad Blocker also won’t block sponsored shortcuts and other sponsored content shown by Firefox when you open a new tab.

Mozilla said another privacy protection already built into Firefox includes Enhanced Tracking Protection, which blocks many trackers and limits tracking across the internet. Ad trackers are methods, such as cookies and tracking pixels, that help companies determine your online preferences and then target you with products they think you might want to buy.

Tech.title: Runway’s New AI Model Creates Digital Worlds Without Code
Tech.content:
The AI company Runway has unveiled a new type of AI model it’s calling an interface world model, allowing you to create interactive websites and more by directly interfacing with elements on screen.

Announced on Monday, the new model, named Solaris, doesn’t require hard programming knowledge to create something new, potentially opening up a new world of design possibilities for those without typical coding skills. This isn’t vibe coding, though — this is live rendering in a way we haven’t seen before.

Runway makes this novel model work by combining reasoning and rendering. Solaris itself generates the interface frame by frame, while a language model “determines how that interface evolves.” The combination of the two enables real-time environments that adapt to how you interact with them.

Solaris generates digital environments in real time, frame by frame, creating applications or other interfaces. When you click on or drag an element, the model will treat these interactions as conditioning signals to generate additional frames. It really needs to be seen to be believed, and if it works as well as some of the demo videos do, we may be at a point where effortless design is within reach for everyone.

Since the model is entirely visual, there are a lot of interesting things you can do with it. Runway gives the example of using an image of yourself as a reference point in a clothing store, where you would simply click on a new shirt on the clothing rack and drag it onto you to see how it looks. This isn’t the first time we’ve seen AI help you try on clothes, but it’s very different from what we’ve seen from Google.

You can also provide text-based prompt instructions, like asking to change the color of an object or move an element in a photo somewhere else.

Solaris essentially feels like a livestreaming video that constantly changes in response to user interaction.

AI world models are expected to be the next big thing, and Solaris is one of the fruits of this next frontier. World models extend themselves beyond the realms of a typical large language model as they’re built to translate and transform our physical world.

The announcement did not specify when Solaris would be available to customers, and Runway did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

Tech.title: Should You Turn Off Your AC When You Go on Vacation? An Expert Explains
Tech.content:
When it’s time to leave for vacation, you know what steps to take: Turn off all the lights, double-check every door is locked and have a neighbor on standby in case any packages are delivered while you’re away. But what about your air conditioner? Should you turn it off, or is there a magic energy-saving temperature you should set it to?

We turned to an HVAC expert for answers. Here’s everything you need to know ahead of your next trip.

Should you turn your air conditioner off when you’re on vacation?

Making small adjustments is the better option. Getty Images

Although turning off your air conditioner while you’re away may seem like a way to save money, it could do more harm than good in the long run.

“If your home overheats, you risk damage to your electronics, losing houseplants and unsafe conditions for pets,” Erin Katz, the operations manager at Allen Service, which provides HVAC, plumbing and electrical services in Colorado, told CNET.

She also pointed out that once you return home from your vacation, your air conditioner will have to work extra hard to get back to a comfortable temperature, which can put extra stress on the system or air conditioning unit.

What is the ideal air conditioner temperature when on vacation?

While you shouldn’t turn off your air conditioner completely, you can slightly adjust its temperature so that it isn’t running consistently while you’re away.

“I recommend setting it a few degrees warmer than you would when you’re at home,” Katz said. “For example, 75 degrees Fahrenheit instead of 70 degrees Fahrenheit.”

This type of adjustment will mean less energy is used, but won’t allow your home to become excruciatingly hot while you’re away.

“The goal is to pick a slightly warmer but stable temperature that your system can maintain without too much trouble while you’re away,” Katz said. “It uses far less energy to make micro adjustments than it does to turn the system on and off, or ask it to make a big change, such as going from 85 degrees Fahrenheit to 70 degrees Fahrenheit when you get home.”

The smart thermostat swap

The Ecobee Smart Thermostat Premium is our favorite smart thermostat thanks to its air quality monitoring, ability to learn your schedule and more. Ecobee/CNET

If you’d rather have full control over your thermostat, even while you’re away, a smart thermostat is the best option.

“They are great for optimizing your energy usage,” Katz explained.

Smart thermostats have connected phone apps, so you can adjust your home’s temperature from anywhere. They also have scheduling features to automate temperature changes, helping keep your home at an ideal temperature and ensuring it never gets too hot or cold, even when you’re away.
